# Everyone Hates Elon: A Comprehensive Analysis of the 2025 Anti-Billionaire Resistance Movement
## Executive Summary
The emergence of the activist collective **Everyone Hates Elon (EHE)** in early 2025 marks a significant pivot in the landscape of 21st-century protest movements. Originating in London, United Kingdom, as a direct response to the perceived political overreach of the billionaire class—specifically Tesla CEO Elon Musk—the group rapidly evolved from a localized "guerrilla marketing" operation into an internationally recognized brand of resistance.

This report provides an exhaustive examination of the group's genesis, operational structure, campaign strategies, and socio-economic impact. By synthesizing data from financial reports, Freedom of Information (FOI) requests, social media analytics, and press coverage, we analyze how a small, anonymous collective utilized the mechanisms of the attention economy to challenge the world's wealthiest individual. The report further explores the group's expansion beyond Musk to target figures such as Jeff Bezos, Donald Trump, and J.D. Vance, situating their activities within the broader "tech-lash" and anti-oligarchy sentiments of the mid-2020s.

## 1\. Socio-Political Genesis
### 1.1 The Context of 2025
To understand the formation of Everyone Hates Elon, one must first analyze the volatile socio-political climate of January 2025\. The global political landscape was characterized by a resurgence of right-wing populism, underscored by the second inauguration of Donald Trump as President of the United States. This period saw an unprecedented convergence of technology, capital, and state power, exemplified by the appointment of Elon Musk to the Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE) .

In the United Kingdom, where the group was founded, public sentiment was increasingly critical of the influence of American tech oligarchs on domestic affairs. Elon Musk’s utilization of his social media platform, X (formerly Twitter), to comment on British riots and support figures like Tommy Robinson had already primed a segment of the British public for opposition .

### 1.2 The Inciting Incident: The Inauguration "Salute"
The singular catalyst for the group's transition from private grievance to public action was the inauguration of Donald Trump in January 2025\. During the televised ceremony, Elon Musk was captured on video and in photographs performing a gesture—a raised arm with a flat palm—that was widely interpreted by critics as resembling a Nazi "Sieg Heil" salute .

While supporters and some commentators argued the gesture was a harmless wave or a "Roman salute," the ambiguity of the action, combined with Musk's previous engagement with far-right memes and rhetoric, served as a flashpoint. For the founders of EHE, this image was not merely a gaffe but a semiotic declaration of alignment with authoritarianism. As noted in later interviews, the founders viewed this moment as the "point of no return," where the distinction between the eccentric billionaire and the political ideologue collapsed .

### 1.3 Formation and Identity
Everyone Hates Elon was formally established in the weeks following the inauguration. The group emerged from what was described as a "ranty group chat" among a small circle of friends in London. Unlike traditional NGOs with boards and formal memberships, EHE adopted a decentralized, anonymous structure typical of Gen Z and Millennial digital activism .

* **The Core Team:** The group is steered by a "handful of people," specifically a core operational team of three individuals. These members maintain strict anonymity to avoid legal retaliation from the litigious billionaire class and harassment from Musk’s fervent online fanbase . 
* **The Mission:** The collective's stated purpose is to "hold Elon Musk to account" and prevent him from "poisoning our politics." They position themselves as a bulwark against the normalization of far-right ideology funded by tech wealth .

## 2\. Organizational Architecture and Financial Model
A defining characteristic of Everyone Hates Elon is its sophisticated approach to resource mobilization. Despite its grassroots origins, the group developed a transparent and highly "gamified" funding model that leveraged the very behaviors they sought to critique.

### 2.1 The "People vs Elon" Fund
The group’s primary financial vehicle is a GoFundMe campaign titled "People vs Elon." By January 2025, the campaign had established a clear operational budget, seeking to raise £50,000 to sustain their activities through the spring of 2025 .

**Table 1: "People vs Elon" Budget Allocation (2025)**

| Category | Allocation (%) | Amount (£) | Purpose |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Core Team Wages** | 63% | £31,500 | Salaries for 3 full-time organizers to design/deliver actions. |
| **Media Production** | 32% | £16,000 | Printing posters, stickers, billboards, and video content. |
| **Admin & Logistics** | 5% | £2,500 | Travel, tools, food, and miscellaneous operational costs. |

Data Source: 8

This transparency regarding "wages" is notable. Unlike many activist groups that rely on volunteer labor, EHE explicitly argued that professionalizing their resistance—allowing organizers to quit their day jobs—was necessary to combat a billionaire with unlimited resources. They framed this as "the power of people" versus "billionaire donors" .

### 2.2 Gamification: The Pledge-Per-Tweet Model
Perhaps the group’s most innovative engagement strategy was the "Pledge Per Tweet" system. Recognizing that Elon Musk posts on X with high frequency (estimated by the group at roughly 2,000 times per month), EHE created a platform where supporters could pledge a micro-donation (e.g., 1p, 2p, 5p) for every tweet Musk published .

* **Mechanism:** A donor pledging 1p per tweet would donate approximately £20 per month. 
* **Psychological Impact:** This model inverted the power dynamic of Musk’s social media addiction. Instead of his tweets generating revenue solely for X (via engagement), they now generated revenue for the group dedicated to his downfall. The group marketed this as "turning every single Elon Musk tweet into a weapon against him" . 
* **Fund Distribution:** Proceeds from this specific stream were designated not just for EHE's operations, but also for donations to causes Musk "hates," such as refugee charities (e.g., Women for Refugee Women) and anti-racist organizations (e.g., Hope not Hate) .

## 3\. The "Swasticar" Campaign: A Semiotic Offensive
In February 2025, Everyone Hates Elon launched its inaugural and most notorious public campaign: The "Swasticar" initiative. This campaign utilized guerrilla marketing tactics to permanently associate the Tesla brand with the imagery of the Nazi regime, capitalizing on the inauguration controversy.

### 3.1 The Neologism and Imagery
The campaign hinged on the creation of the portmanteau **"Swasticar"** (Swastika \+ Car). This linguistic device served as a sticky meme, transforming every Tesla vehicle into a mobile billboard for the group's critique.

* **Visual Design:** The primary poster featured a high-contrast black-and-white image of Elon Musk at the inauguration, arm raised. The typography mimicked the sleek, sans-serif aesthetic of modern tech advertising, creating a dissonance between the corporate style and the fascist content . 
* **The Slogan:** "Goes from 0 to 1939 in 3 seconds." This tag line cleverly subverted the standard automotive performance metric (0 to 60 mph) to reference the year Nazi Germany invaded Poland, marking the start of World War II. The joke operated on two levels: criticizing the speed of the car and the speed of Musk’s political radicalization .

### 3.2 Deployment Vectors
The campaign was multi-modal, targeting both fixed infrastructure and mobile assets.

#### 3.2.1 The Transit Infiltration (TfL)
Activists infiltrated the Transport for London (TfL) network, opening locked advertising cabinets at bus stops and on London Underground carriages to replace legitimate advertisements with EHE posters.

* **Locations:** High-visibility areas including Bethnal Green, Walthamstow, Clerkenwell, and the Victoria Line . 
* **Variations:** 
 * *The Financial Critique:* A graph showing Tesla's plummeting stock with the text "Hate doesn't sell. Just ask Tesla" . 
 * *The Insult:* A stark poster reading "Elon Musk is a bellend. Signed, the UK" . 
 * *The Cinematic Spoof:* A mock movie poster for "The Fast and Führer," depicted a Doge-plated Tesla Model S with the caption "Heil Tesla" .

#### 3.2.2 The Sticker Intifada
Simultaneously, the group released print-at-home templates for "Don't Buy a Swasticar" stickers via Instagram. This democratized the activism, allowing followers to tag Tesla vehicles in their own neighborhoods. The group claimed hundreds of Teslas in London were tagged, effectively turning the product against its owner .

#### 3.2.3 Merchandise and Accessories
The group extended the campaign into satirical consumer goods, producing "Musk B-Gone" car air fresheners with the tagline "covers the stench of fascism." These were distributed to supporters and placed in shops, further embedding the narrative into everyday commerce .

### 3.3 The Showroom Confrontation
In a direct confrontation, the core team carried a life-sized cardboard cutout of the "saluting" Musk into a flagship Tesla showroom in North London. The action was filmed and uploaded to TikTok, showing staff and customers reacting with hostility. The group reported that customers told them to "f\*ck off," a reaction EHE cited as evidence that they had successfully pierced the bubble of the brand's prestige .

## 4\. Institutional Response and Legal Repercussions
The aggressive nature of the "Swasticar" campaign provoked significant responses from state authorities and corporate bodies, revealing the legal and ethical boundaries of the group's methodology.

### 4.1 Transport for London (TfL) and Police Action
TfL took a hardline stance against the campaign. In internal emails released via Freedom of Information (FOI) requests, TfL officials described the posters as "criminal damage" and "illegal flyposting."

* **Rapid Removal:** TfL coordinated with their advertising partner, JCDecaux, to "expeditiously remove" the posters. The agency also engaged with the British Transport Police regarding the security breaches that allowed activists to access locked ad spaces . 
* **Bureaucratic Panic:** The FOI documents reveal a flurry of internal communication, with subject lines like "FW: Fake Posters \- Anti-Musk/Anti-Tesla," highlighting the urgency with which the transport authority viewed the reputational risk .

### 4.2 The Antisemitism Controversy
A critical dimension of the institutional response came from Jewish advocacy groups. Internal TfL correspondence noted that a "Jewish security organisation" had contacted the authority to express concern.

* **The Critique:** The organization highlighted that "any reference to Nazi salutes or swastikas is understandably triggering for the Jewish community," regardless of the satirical intent. This raised a complex ethical question for EHE: in their zeal to label Musk a fascist, were they inadvertently utilizing hate speech imagery that harmed the very minorities they claimed to support?.12

## 5\. "London vs Musk": The Aesthetics of Destruction
Following the viral success of the poster campaign, EHE pivoted to performance art. On April 10, 2025, the group staged an event titled **"London vs Musk"** in South London, which introduced a visceral, physical element to their digital-first activism.

### 5.1 The Event Mechanics
The centerpiece of the event was a used Tesla Model S, which the group claimed was "donated anonymously" and was already destined for the scrapyard. This framing was crucial to deflect accusations of environmental waste or wanton vandalism .

* **Participation:** Members of the public were invited to take turns smashing the vehicle with sledgehammers, crowbars, and other tools. The event was billed as a "public art piece" designed to allow citizens to "vent their rage" at the billionaire class safely and legally .

### 5.2 Theoretical Framework: Destruction Art
The event drew clear parallels to the tradition of "Destruction Art" (e.g., Gustav Metzger), where the annihilation of an object serves as a critique of the system that produced it. By physically dismantling a Tesla—the ultimate status symbol of the eco-conscious elite—participants were symbolically dismantling the myth of ethical consumption under capitalism.

### 5.3 Philanthropic Component
To further legitimize the violence of the act, the group announced that the scrap metal and battery would be recycled, and the "remains" of the vehicle would be auctioned. All proceeds were pledged to food bank charities, reinforcing the group's narrative contrast between Musk’s $200 billion wealth and the hunger of British nurses .

### 5.4 Safety and Legal Disclaimers
Cognizant of the potential for copycat crimes, EHE issued stern warnings alongside the event coverage. A spokesperson stated, "We absolutely do not condone damage to any other vehicles... you would face serious legal consequences." This disclaimer highlighted the tension between their incendiary rhetoric ("Don't buy a Swasticar") and the need to avoid liability for widespread criminal damage .

## 6\. Strategic Expansion: Targeting the Oligarchy
As 2025 progressed, Everyone Hates Elon expanded its target list. The group recognized that Musk was merely the most visible symptom of a broader systemic issue: the unchecked power of the ultra-wealthy.

### 6.1 The Siege of Venice: Jeff Bezos (June 2025\)
In June 2025, the group targeted Amazon founder Jeff Bezos during his wedding to Lauren Sánchez in Venice, Italy.

* **Coalition Building:** EHE collaborated with Greenpeace Italy and a local collective called "No Space for Bezos." This marked a significant step in internationalizing their operations . 
* **The Tactics:** Activists unfurled a massive banner in St. Mark's Square and threatened to disrupt the wedding procession on the canals using "whatever can float," including inflatable crocodiles. The protest focused on Amazon's labor practices and carbon footprint . 
* **Outcome:** The threat of disruption was credible enough that Bezos and Sánchez reportedly altered their wedding reception plans to avoid the protesters, a victory EHE claimed as proof of their disruptive capacity .

### 6.2 The State Visit: Donald Trump and Jeffrey Epstein (September 2025\)
Anticipating Donald Trump’s state visit to the UK in September 2025, EHE launched a campaign focused on the President's past association with convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein.

* **Windsor Castle:** Less than 24 hours before Trump’s arrival, the group unfurled a "supersized" photo of Trump and Epstein on the grounds outside Windsor Castle. The location was chosen to maximize embarrassment for the Royal Family and the visiting delegation . 
* **Aberdeen Golf Course:** In Scotland, the group drove a van emblazoned with the Trump/Epstein image around the perimeter of Trump’s golf course while he met with UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer. They also installed a parody "memorial plaque" on a bench at the course . 
* **Crowdfunding:** This specific sub-campaign raised over £32,000, demonstrating the public's willingness to fund anti-Trump actions specifically .

### 6.3 Domestic Targets: Jim Ratcliffe and J.D. Vance
The group also targeted British billionaire Sir Jim Ratcliffe (CEO of INEOS) and U.S. Vice President J.D. Vance.

* **Ratcliffe:** Posters featuring Ratcliffe appeared alongside Musk, criticizing his tax practices and environmental record . 
* **Vance:** During a UK visit, EHE utilized a billboard in Cheltenham to declare Vance "NOT welcome," citing his "far-right friends" and the starvation in Palestine as reasons he should not be afforded British hospitality .

## 7\. Economic Impact Analysis: The "Tesla Takedown"
A central claim of the EHE campaign is that their actions materially damaged Tesla's financial standing. While establishing direct causality in stock markets is difficult, the correlation between the group's peak activity and Tesla's 2025 slump is notable.

### 7.1 Financial Performance in 2025
Data from early 2025 indicates a severe downturn for Tesla, Inc.

* **Stock Price:** Tesla stock plummeted from a high of $479.86 in late 2024 to a low of $281.95 in February 2025—the exact month of the "Swasticar" campaign launch . 
* **Sales Volume:** In January 2025, Tesla sales in Europe dropped by nearly 50%. By March 2025, the European Automobile Manufacturers' Association reported a further 40% year-on-year decline .

### 7.2 Attribution of Losses
Financial analysts have debated the drivers of this collapse.

* **The EHE Argument:** The group claims their "Swasticar" branding and the "London vs Musk" stunts made the car socially toxic. They argue that for the liberal, urban demographic that buys EVs, driving a "Swasticar" became a social liability . 
* **The Analyst View:** Market analysts at firms like Wedbush and William Blair acknowledged that Musk’s "political toxicity" was a major factor. They noted that Musk’s involvement in the Trump administration (DOGE) and his "far-right politics" alienated the core customer base. While they did not always name EHE specifically, they cited the "brand damage" that EHE was actively manufacturing . 
* **Market Context:** Other factors, such as the rise of Chinese EVs and the broader rotation out of "Magnificent Seven" tech stocks, also contributed to the decline .

However, the specific collapse in *European* sales, where EHE was most active, suggests the group played a catalysing role in turning vague dissatisfaction into an active consumer boycott .

## 8\. Global Ripple Effects and Copycat Movements
The success of Everyone Hates Elon inspired a wave of similar actions globally, creating a decentralized network of anti-Musk resistance.

* **Tesla Takedown:** A broader umbrella term used by activists in the US and Europe. 
* **The Cybertruck Hunters:** A TikTok-based group that projected anti-Musk videos onto the flat rear tailgates of Tesla Cybertrucks in major US cities . 
* **San Francisco Protests:** In Musk’s home turf, protesters gathered at showrooms chanting "Elon Musk has got to go" and unfurled banners reading "No Swasticars," directly adopting the language coined by the London group . 
* **Paris Effigies:** In April 2025, concurrent with the London sledgehammer event, protesters in Paris burned a cardboard effigy of a Tesla during a demonstration .

## 9\. Conclusion
Everyone Hates Elon represents a new paradigm in corporate accountability activism. By fusing the irreverence of internet culture with the physical disruption of traditional protest, the group successfully punctured the aura of invincibility surrounding the world's richest man.

While their methods—particularly the use of Nazi imagery—remained controversial, their impact on Tesla's brand equity in the UK and Europe was palpable. The group demonstrated that in the age of the attention economy, a small, underfunded collective could inflict billions of dollars in reputational damage by simply refusing to let a billionaire control the narrative. As of late 2025, with Tesla's stock still struggling to recover its previous highs and Musk’s political entanglements deepening, the campaign shows no signs of abating.

| Date | Event | Location | Key Details | Source |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Jan 20** | **The Catalyst** | Washington D.C. | Musk performs controversial salute at Trump Inauguration. | 6 |
| **Feb 1** | **Campaign Launch** | London | "Swasticar" posters appear in TfL network. | 1 |
| **Feb 24** | **Viral Peak** | Online | "0 to 1939" slogan trends; 6M+ views on TikTok. | 2 |
| **Mar 06** | **TfL Crackdown** | London | TfL confirms removal of "unauthorized" posters. | 12 |
| **Apr 10** | **London vs Musk** | South London | Public destruction of Tesla Model S with sledgehammers. | 4 |
| **Jun 23** | **Venice Wedding** | Venice, Italy | Protest at Bezos wedding; "No Space for Bezos" banner. | 19 |
| **Sep 15** | **Trump Visit** | Windsor/Aberdeen | Trump/Epstein banner at Windsor Castle; Van stunt. | 21 |

**Table 3: Tesla Stock vs. EHE Activity (Early 2025\)**

| Period | Tesla Stock Trend | EHE Activity Level | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Dec 2024** | High ($479.86) | None | Pre-Campaign peak. |
| **Jan 2025** | Declining | Formation | Musk appointment to DOGE; Inauguration salute. |
| **Feb 2025** | Plunging ($281.95) | **High (Swasticar)** | Poster campaign goes viral; "Swasticar" enters lexicon. |
| **Mar 2025** | Stagnant/Low | Medium | Showroom confrontations; Sales down 40% in EU. |
| **Apr 2025** | Low ($291.00) | **High (Sledgehammer)** | Physical destruction events; Paris protests. |

The group also targeted British billionaire Sir Jim Ratcliffe (CEO of INEOS) and U.S. Vice President J.D. Vance.
Posters featuring Sir Jim Ratcliffe appeared alongside Musk, criticizing his tax practices and environmental record.

During a UK visit, EHE utilized a billboard in Cheltenham to declare Vance "NOT welcome," citing his "far-right friends" and the starvation in Palestine as reasons he should not be afforded British hospitality.
A central claim of the EHE campaign is that their actions materially damaged Tesla's financial standing.
Data from early 2025 indicates a severe downturn for Tesla, Inc.
Tesla stock plummeted from a high of $479.86 in late 2024 to a low of $281.95 in February 2025—the exact month of the "Swasticar" campaign launch.
In January 2025, Tesla sales in Europe dropped by nearly 50%.
By March 2025, the European Automobile Manufacturers' Association reported a further 40% year-on-year decline in Tesla sales.
Financial analysts have debated the drivers of Tesla's collapse.
The EHE group claims their "Swasticar" branding and the "London vs Musk" stunts made the car socially toxic.
EHE argues that for the liberal, urban demographic that buys EVs, driving a "Swasticar" became a social liability.
Market analysts at firms like Wedbush and William Blair acknowledged that Musk’s "political toxicity" was a major factor in Tesla's decline.
Analysts noted that Musk’s involvement in the Trump administration (DOGE) and his "far-right politics" alienated the core customer base.
Other factors, such as the rise of Chinese EVs and the broader rotation out of "Magnificent Seven" tech stocks, also contributed to Tesla's decline.
The specific collapse in European Tesla sales, where EHE was most active, suggests the group played a catalysing role in turning vague dissatisfaction into an active consumer boycott.
The success of Everyone Hates Elon inspired a wave of similar actions globally, creating a decentralized network of anti-Musk resistance.
A broader umbrella term used by activists in the US and Europe is "Tesla Takedown."
The Cybertruck Hunters is a TikTok-based group that projected anti-Musk videos onto the flat rear tailgates of Tesla Cybertrucks in major US cities.
In Musk’s home turf, protesters gathered at showrooms chanting "Elon Musk has got to go" and unfurled banners reading "No Swasticars," directly adopting the language coined by the London group.
In April 2025, concurrent with the London sledgehammer event, protesters in Paris burned a cardboard effigy of a Tesla during a demonstration.
Everyone Hates Elon represents a new paradigm in corporate accountability activism.
By fusing the irreverence of internet culture with the physical disruption of traditional protest, the group successfully punctured the aura of invincibility surrounding the world's richest man.
While their methods—particularly the use of Nazi imagery—remained controversial, their impact on Tesla's brand equity in the UK and Europe was palpable.

The group demonstrated that in the age of the attention economy, a small, underfunded collective could inflict billions of dollars in reputational damage by simply refusing to let a billionaire control the narrative.
As of late 2025, with Tesla's stock still struggling to recover its previous highs and Musk’s political entanglements deepening, the campaign shows no signs of abating.

4.title: Everyone Hates Elon
4.content:
[![Image 1: This is a good article. Click here for more information.](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/9/94/Symbol_support_vote.svg/20px-Symbol_support_vote.svg.png)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Good_articles* "This is a good article. Click here for more information.")

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

Everyone Hates Elon| Formation | 2025 |
| --- |
| Purpose | [Protesting against Elon Musk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protests_against_Elon_Musk "Protests against Elon Musk") and other [billionaires](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billionaire "Billionaire") |
| Location | * [London](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London "London"), United Kingdom |
| Methods | * [Guerrilla marketing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guerrilla_marketing "Guerrilla marketing") * [Billboard hacking](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_hacking "Billboard hacking") * [Subvertising](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Subvertising "Subvertising") |
| Website | [peoplevselon.co.uk](http://peoplevselon.co.uk/) |

**Everyone Hates Elon** is a British [political campaign](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Political_campaign "Political campaign") group. The group formed in 2025 to voice opposition to businessman and [US presidential advisor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Senior_Advisor_to_the_President_of_the_United_States "Senior Advisor to the President of the United States")[Elon Musk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elon_Musk "Elon Musk"), citing his behaviour in the [Department of Government Efficiency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Department_of_Government_Efficiency "Department of Government Efficiency"), his [statements about British politics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_relations_of_Elon_Musk#United_Kingdom "International relations of Elon Musk"), and promotion of [disinformation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disinformation "Disinformation"). The group creates humorous [parody advertisements](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Subvertising "Subvertising") and [viral](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Viral_marketing "Viral marketing") social media campaigns to communicate their critiques of Musk and other [billionaires](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billionaire "Billionaire"). Their activities have included distributing [posters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Poster "Poster") criticising Musk and [Jeff Bezos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeff_Bezos "Jeff Bezos"), as well as establishing a [fundraising](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fundraising "Fundraising") campaign in support of "causes [Musk] hates".[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-NewYorker-Russell-1) The group also organised an interactive protest event where participants were invited to destroy a [Tesla Model S](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tesla_Model_S "Tesla Model S") to raise money for [food banks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Food_bank "Food bank").

Everyone Hates Elon formed in early 2025 in response to Musk's interest in British affairs, including [his support](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Political_activities_of_Elon_Musk#Reform_UK "Political activities of Elon Musk") for [far-right](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Far-right_politics "Far-right politics") activist and [anti-Islam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anti-Islam_sentiment "Anti-Islam sentiment") campaigner [Tommy Robinson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tommy_Robinson "Tommy Robinson"), as well as [Musk's salute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elon_Musk_salute_controversy "Elon Musk salute controversy")—interpreted by many as a Nazi salute—at the [second inauguration of Donald Trump](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_inauguration_of_Donald_Trump "Second inauguration of Donald Trump").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-THR-Ford-2) The group began as a "ranty group chat" among a small group of friends,[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-NewYorker-Russell-1) and is currently made up of "just a handful of people",[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-THR-Ford-2) with members choosing to remain anonymous.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-NewYorker-Russell-1) They told _[The Hollywood Reporter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Hollywood\_Reporter "The Hollywood Reporter")_ that they were working to "piss off Elon Musk one small action at a time", and that their campaigns targeting [Tesla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tesla,_Inc. "Tesla, Inc.") were intended to encourage the public to express their opposition to Musk by [withdrawing their support](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dollar_voting "Dollar voting") from the company, which is the main source of Musk's wealth.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-THR-Ford-2) In an interview with Anna Russell for _[The New Yorker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_New\_Yorker "The New Yorker")_, Everyone Hates Elon founders described their strategy of using memorable, humorous [slogans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slogan "Slogan") to combat the catchy [political messaging](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Political_communication "Political communication") used by the far-right; they explained, "We can't outspend [Musk]... but we know that we're funnier than him. He's definitely not funny."[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-NewYorker-Russell-1) They also described their confusion as to Musk's motives for becoming involved in UK politics; Russell noted that a 2025 [YouGov](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/YouGov "YouGov") poll, which reported that eighty percent of British people had unfavourable opinions of Elon Musk,[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-YouGov-Smith-3) indicates that the group's "dislike" of the billionaire is shared by a majority of the UK public.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-NewYorker-Russell-1)

Everyone Hates Elon's first action was to create a fundraising campaign, titled _People Versus Elon_, which allows donors to pledge one penny ([£](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pound_sterling "Pound sterling")0.01) every time Musk posts on [X](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twitter "Twitter"), with all funds to be donated to causes that Musk dislikes.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-NewYorker-Russell-1) These include organisations such as [Women for Refugee Women](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Women_for_Refugee_Women "Women for Refugee Women"), [Hope not Hate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hope_not_Hate "Hope not Hate"), and Rainbow Migration, a charity supporting [LGBTQI+](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LGBTQ_community "LGBTQ community")[asylum seekers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asylum_seekers "Asylum seekers").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-LFF-Barber1-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-RainbowMigration2025-5) The campaign, which is anticipated to raise £150,000 over the course of one year,[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-NewYorker-Russell-1) was discussed in a February 2025 episode of _[The Guilty Feminist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Guilty\_Feminist "The Guilty Feminist")_ podcast.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-THR-Ford-2)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-GuiltyFeminist-6)

Everyone Hates Elon rose to further prominence in February 2025 when they began a [guerrilla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guerrilla_marketing "Guerrilla marketing") poster campaign, installing posters criticising Elon Musk around London; one poster read "Elon Musk is a [bellend](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/bell-end "wikt:bell-end"). Signed, the UK".[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-NewYorker-Russell-1) Several posters were designed as [parody advertisements](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Subvertising "Subvertising") for [Tesla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tesla,_Inc. "Tesla, Inc."),[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-Independent-Butler1-7) carrying the Tesla [wordmark](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wordmark "Wordmark") accompanied by the [parody](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parody "Parody") tagline "The [Swasticar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swasticar "Swasticar")".[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-Euronews-Mouriquand-8) These posters displayed slogans including "Goes from 0 to 1939 in 3 seconds", "Now with White Power Steering",[[a]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-9) and "[Autopilot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tesla_Autopilot "Tesla Autopilot") for your car. [Autocrat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Autocracy "Autocracy") for your country."[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-PinkNews-Billson-10)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-Independent-Butler1-7) The posters [covered existing advertisements](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_hacking "Billboard hacking") at [bus shelters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bus_stop "Bus stop") in [Clerkenwell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clerkenwell "Clerkenwell") and [Bethnal Green](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bethnal_Green "Bethnal Green").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-Independent-Butler1-7)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-Euronews-Mouriquand-8)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-NYT-Shear-11) The group also produced and distributed posters targeting Musk-owned [social networking service](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Social_networking_service "Social networking service") X (formerly [Twitter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twitter "Twitter")); the posters showed an image of [Musk doing a Nazi-like salute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elon_Musk_salute_controversy "Elon Musk salute controversy"). One design carried the slogan "X marks the rot"[[b]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-12) and another read "Delete your account. If the bar lets Nazis in, it's a Nazi bar."[[c]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-13)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-MyLondon-Holden-14) In an advertisement mimicking a [public health](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Public_health "Public health") information poster using the [NHS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Health_Service "National Health Service") logo, Everyone Hates Elon called on the public to recognise [parasites](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parasitism "Parasitism"), and listed as examples [ticks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tick "Tick"), [worms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parasitic_worm "Parasitic worm"), and [billionaires](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billionaire "Billionaire").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-NewYorker-Russell-1)

Alongside the [street furniture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Street_furniture "Street furniture") poster campaign, Everyone Hates Elon installed banners on [London Underground](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London_Underground "London Underground") trains. One of these posters carried the phrase "Hate doesn't sell. Just ask Elon Musk", alongside an image of image of [Musk's salute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elon_Musk_salute_controversy "Elon Musk salute controversy") and a graphic of Tesla's declining [share price](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Share_price "Share price").[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-LFF-Mahmood1-15)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-Independent-Butler1-7)[Transport for London](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transport_for_London "Transport for London") later confirmed that the group's posters "were not authorised" to be put up on the network, and that unauthorised posters would be "expeditiously removed".[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-MyLondon-Holden-14)[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-NewYorker-Russell-1)

Everyone Hates Elon also created and distributed stickers saying "Don't Buy a Swasticar", and shared the sticker templates with their followers on [Instagram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Instagram "Instagram").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-Euronews-Mouriquand-8) The group also turned the image of Musk's Nazi salute into a [life-sized cutout](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Standee "Standee"), and installed it in a North London [Tesla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tesla,_Inc. "Tesla, Inc.") showroom.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-NewYorker-Russell-1) They created a range of [Car Freshners](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Car_Freshner "Car Freshner") with the slogan "Musk B-Gone" and tagline "covers the stench of fascism".[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-LFF-Mahmood2-16)

### Jeff Bezos and Amazon

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Everyone_Hates_Elon&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Jeff Bezos and Amazon")]

On 14 April 2025, singer [Katy Perry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Katy_Perry "Katy Perry") was part of [a space flight](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blue_Origin_NS-31 "Blue Origin NS-31") run by [Blue Origin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blue_Origin "Blue Origin"), a [space technology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Space_technology "Space technology") company founded by billionaire [Jeff Bezos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeff_Bezos "Jeff Bezos").[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-Guardian-Helmore-17) Bezos also founded [Amazon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amazon_(company) "Amazon (company)"), and both his own [tax avoidance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tax_avoidance "Tax avoidance") and that of Amazon have been the subject of criticism for several years.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-ProPublica2021-18)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-Guardian-Neate-19) Following the space flight, Everyone Hates Elon produced posters targeting Bezos and Perry. One, which was installed near Amazon's [UK headquarters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Amazon_locations#Other_major_campuses "List of Amazon locations") in [Shoreditch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shoreditch "Shoreditch"), read "If you can afford to send Katy Perry to space, you can afford to pay more taxes."[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-LFF-Barber2-20) The group also installed posters featuring Perry outside a branch of [Amazon Fresh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amazon_Fresh "Amazon Fresh") in [Angel, London](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angel,_London "Angel, London"); these posters carried the Amazon logo alongside the caption "Our tax avoidance is out of this world, just ask Katy Perry."[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-LFF-Barber2-20)

In June 2025, Everyone Hates Elon collaborated with [Greenpeace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greenpeace "Greenpeace") to protest against the [wedding of Jeff Bezos and Lauren Sánchez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wedding_of_Jeff_Bezos_and_Lauren_S%C3%A1nchez "Wedding of Jeff Bezos and Lauren Sánchez"). The wedding, held in [Venice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Venice "Venice"), Italy, had already attracted opposition from residents of the city, and protests were held in the weeks leading up to the event by a local group called "No Space for Bezos".[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-BBC-RainsfordGhiglione-21) On 23 June, activists from Everyone Hates Elon and Greenpeace unfurled a large banner, measuring 20 by 20 m (66 by 66 ft),[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-France24-Venice-22) in [Piazza San Marco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piazza_San_Marco "Piazza San Marco"); the banner featured an image of Bezos laughing, along with the slogan "If you can rent Venice for your wedding you can pay more tax."[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-Variety-Vivarelli-23)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-Guardian-Giuffrida-24) A statement from the two groups explained that although Bezos is one of the wealthiest people in the world, he "is reported to pay a 1.1% true [tax rate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tax_rate "Tax rate")",[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-Variety-Vivarelli-23) and that the aim of the protest was to highlight the comparatively low tax contributions of billionaires, who nonetheless "exacerbat[e] the climate crisis with environmentally unsustainable lifestyles".[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-ABCNews-AP-25)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-ITVNews-Greenpeace-26) The banner was soon removed by [local police](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polizia_Locale "Polizia Locale").[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-LATimes-AP-27) In response to the protests, the [Mayor of Venice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mayor_of_Venice "Mayor of Venice"), [Luigi Brugnaro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luigi_Brugnaro "Luigi Brugnaro"), said he was "ashamed of the protesters"[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-GPB-Treisman-28) and defended the wedding, highlighting the financial gain that the event offered to the city; local activists argued that Venice needs "public services and housing, not VIPs and [over-tourism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Overtourism "Overtourism")."[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-Reuters-KucukgocmenArmellini-29) Simone Venturini, the city's councillor for [tourism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tourism "Tourism"), claimed that the protests were motivated by "social envy" and "a desire for media attention".[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-NPR-Treisman-30) Eventually, the location of the wedding's main [reception](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wedding_reception "Wedding reception") was moved from its planned venue, [Scuola Grande della Misericordia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scuola_vecchia_della_Misericordia "Scuola vecchia della Misericordia"), to the [Venetian Arsenal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Venetian_Arsenal "Venetian Arsenal") further from the centre of the city;[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGaffneyKerrigan202500:01:18%E2%80%9300:01:38-31)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-BBC-RainsfordGhiglione-21) the move was prompted by protestors "threatening to flood the nearby canals with inflatable crocodiles to prevent [the] guests arriving".[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGaffneyKerrigan202500:01:18%E2%80%9300:01:38-31)

### Donald Trump and Jeffrey Epstein

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Everyone_Hates_Elon&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Donald Trump and Jeffrey Epstein")]

In July 2025, it was announced that [Donald Trump](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donald_Trump "Donald Trump") would make two visits to the United Kingdom in the coming months; he visited Scotland later that month,[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-BBC-Delaney-32)[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-BBC-LystO'Hare-33) and a formal [state visit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/State_visit "State visit") with [King Charles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_III "Charles III") took place at [Windsor Castle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Windsor_Castle "Windsor Castle") in September.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-Guardian-Stacey-34)[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-Time-Sutherland1-35) Following the announcement of these visits, and against a backdrop of [recent developments](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donald_Trump_sexual_misconduct_allegations#2025_developments "Donald Trump sexual misconduct allegations") concerning [Trump's relationship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Relationship_of_Donald_Trump_and_Jeffrey_Epstein "Relationship of Donald Trump and Jeffrey Epstein") with convicted [sex offender](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sex_offender "Sex offender")[Jeffrey Epstein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeffrey_Epstein "Jeffrey Epstein"), Everyone Hates Elon installed a poster featuring a large photograph of Trump with Epstein[[d]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-37) on a bus stop in [Nine Elms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nine_Elms "Nine Elms"), close to the [US Embassy in London](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/US_Embassy_in_London "US Embassy in London").[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-Time-Sutherland1-35)[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-Independent-Dobkin-38) Later, the group placed a placard with the phrase "[Twinned](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sister_city "Sister city") with [Epstein Island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Epstein_Island "Epstein Island")" beneath the entrance sign at [Trump International Golf Links](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trump_International_Golf_Links,_Scotland "Trump International Golf Links, Scotland") in [Aberdeenshire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aberdeenshire "Aberdeenshire").[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-Time-Sutherland1-35)[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-Independent-Patrick1-39)

During Trump's visit to Scotland, while he and UK Prime Minister [Keir Starmer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Keir_Starmer "Keir Starmer") were meeting at [Trump's Turnberry golf resort](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trump_Turnberry "Trump Turnberry"), Everyone Hates Elon drove a [mobile billboard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mobile_billboard "Mobile billboard") around [Aberdeen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aberdeen "Aberdeen"); the billboard showed the photograph of Trump and Epstein, along with the phrase "Welcome to Scotland, Donald".[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-Independent-Patrick2-40)[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-STV-VanReenen-41) The group stated that they had "tried to get close to Trump's golf course" with the van but had been stopped by police.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-STV-VanReenen-41)

In September 2025, prior to [Trump's state visit to the UK](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_state_visit_by_Donald_Trump_to_the_United_Kingdom "2025 state visit by Donald Trump to the United Kingdom"), Everyone Hates Elon again displayed the photograph of Trump and Epstein on a bus stop in Nine Elms, this time superimposed with [a 2002 quote](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Relationship_of_Donald_Trump_and_Jeffrey_Epstein#Early_2000s "Relationship of Donald Trump and Jeffrey Epstein") in which Trump praised Epstein and commented on their shared preference for "women... on the younger side".[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-Time-Sutherland2-42)[[e]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-44) On the same bus stop, the group later installed a poster that simply read "Donald Trump is a rapist".[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-ABS-Shelby-45) They installed another plaque at Trump's Aberdeenshire golf course, this time a spoof memorial dedicated to Epstein,[[f]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-47)[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-TheNational-Walker-48) and distributed [merchandise](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Merchandise "Merchandise") featuring the photograph of Trump and Epstein among the products in the [gift shop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gift_shop "Gift shop") at [Windsor Castle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Windsor_Castle "Windsor Castle").[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-Independent-Bishop2-49)

The day before Trump arrived in the UK for the state visit, Everyone Hates Elon unfurled a 400-square-metre (4,300 sq ft)[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-Bracknell-Harris-50) print of the photograph of Trump and Epstein on the lawn of Windsor Castle.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-Time-Sutherland2-42) In a post on Instagram documenting the unveiling of the large banner, the group said that the production of the print was "[crowdfunded](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crowdfunding "Crowdfunding")" by "the British public",[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-Global-Goodman-51) referring to a fundraiser which attracted over £32,000 in donations to Everyone Hates Elon; a spokesperson for the group said their goal was "to make sure Epstein haunts [Trump] everywhere he goes".[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-Hyperallergic-Pontone-52) Later that week, on the day of Trump's arrival at Windsor Castle, the group again used a large mobile billboard van to display the photograph of Trump and Epstein. The van was [stopped by police](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Traffic_stop "Traffic stop") as it was driving around [Windsor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Windsor,_Berkshire "Windsor, Berkshire");[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-Reuters-17Sep-53) Everyone Hates Elon said in an Instagram post that the police had "confiscated" the van and "detained two journalists covering it".[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-Independent-Patrick3-54)[Thames Valley Police](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thames_Valley_Police "Thames Valley Police") later said that the van had been stopped as part of a "security check"[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-Guardian-Sparrow-55) related to the state visit, and that "[n]o arrests were made and no vehicles were seized."[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-Independent-Patrick3-54)

In August 2025, [US Vice President](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/US_Vice_President "US Vice President")[JD Vance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/JD_Vance "JD Vance") visited the UK with his family. The trip included several official engagements, such as a visit with [Foreign Secretary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Foreign_Secretary_(United_Kingdom) "Foreign Secretary (United Kingdom)")[David Lammy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Lammy "David Lammy") at [Chevening](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chevening "Chevening") in [Kent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kent "Kent"). Following this visit, the family travelled to the [Cotswolds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cotswolds "Cotswolds"),[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-Reuters-Renshaw-56) where they stayed at Dean Manor, a [grade II listed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grade_II_listed "Grade II listed")[manor house](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manor_house "Manor house") in [Dean, Oxfordshire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dean,_Oxfordshire "Dean, Oxfordshire").[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-Telegraph-Montgomery-57) During the Vances' stay, which was met with protest from local residents,[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-Guardian-Morris-58) Everyone Hates Elon displayed "a now-infamous [meme](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Internet_meme "Internet meme") of the vice president with a digitally enlarged bald head"[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-People-Kile-59) on another mobile billboard; this was then driven around [Charlbury](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlbury "Charlbury"), close to where the family were staying.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-People-Kile-59)[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-Independent-Bishop1-60) The group also installed the same image on a large billboard in [Cheltenham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cheltenham "Cheltenham").[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-GL-Norris-61) In an Instagram post, Everyone Hates Elon stated that the campaign was intended to show Vance that he was "NOT welcome in the U.K.", further explaining that they "couldn't allow him to dine at expensive restaurants, while [people in Palestine starve to death](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaza_Strip_famine "Gaza Strip famine")... [they] couldn't stand by as he freely hangs out with his [far right](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Far-right_politics "Far-right politics") friends, while taking freedoms away [from] his people".[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-People-Kile-59) The group also launched a [crowdfunding](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crowdfunding "Crowdfunding") campaign, raising funds to help them "ruin JD Vance's trip".[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-People-Kile-59)

On 10 April 2025, Everyone Hates Elon held a one-off [participatory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Participatory_art "Participatory art")[protest art](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protest_art "Protest art") event, titled 'London vs Musk', in [South London](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_London "South London"). During the event, members of the public destroyed a [Tesla Model S](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tesla_Model_S "Tesla Model S"), which had been donated anonymously for the purpose.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-Guardian-McCusker-62) The car was non-functioning and would otherwise have been [scrapped](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vehicle_recycling "Vehicle recycling"); its battery had already been [recycled](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battery_recycling "Battery recycling").[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-Guardian-McCusker-62)[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-NewYorker-Russell-1)

Everyone Hates Elon described the event as a "[public art](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Public_art "Public art") piece"[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-Independent-Campbell-63) allowing participants to express their frustration with the behaviour of Musk and other billionaires and show their opposition to the growth of the far right.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-Guardian-McCusker-62) The event was described by _[The New Yorker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_New\_Yorker "The New Yorker")_ as an "outdoor '[rage room](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rage_room "Rage room")'";[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-NewYorker-Russell-1) around 100 participants were allowed access to the car for 30 seconds each,[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-NewYorker-Russell-1) and used [baseball bats](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baseball_bat "Baseball bat") and [sledgehammers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sledgehammer "Sledgehammer") to destroy the vehicle.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-APNews-64) They also [spray-painted](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spray_painting "Spray painting") the car's bodywork with phrases criticising Musk, expressing dislike of [billionaires](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billionaire "Billionaire") in general, and calling for [wealth taxation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wealth_tax "Wealth tax").[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-Independent-Murray-65)

Following its destruction, the vehicle will be [crushed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Car_crusher "Car crusher") and auctioned, with proceeds to be donated to [food bank](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Food_bank "Food bank") charities.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-Barrons-Gerardy-66)[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-LeFigaro-Dreer-67)[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-NewYorker-Russell-1) A spokesperson for Everyone Hates Elon explained that the group sees a connection between record numbers of billionaires and record numbers of food banks.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-Independent-Campbell-63) They said that the art was "a symbol of resistance to billionaire influence".[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-Standard-Phillips-68)

'Everyone Hates Elon' Protest Group Continue Their Guerilla Campaign Against Trump's Favourite Tech Bro
=======================================================================================================

LONDON, ENGLAND - MARCH 13: The latest in a series of posters critical of Elon Musk that have been unofficially placed in bus shelter advertising frames, stands on March 13, 2025 in London, England. The latest reads "Tesla The Swasticar. Now With White Power Steering" and features a photo of US President Donald Trump promoting the brand of cars with Musk, from a photo-call that took place outside the White House. 'Everyone Hates Elon Musk' are a UK-based collective who have become an online sensation in recent weeks, racking up 10 million-plus views on Tik Tok, due to posters they put up across London picturing Musk making his Hitler-like salute standing in a Tesla or "swasticar", as they have re-christened it. A spokesperson for the group says, "This is a real moment where people have had enough of billionaires getting involved in our politics" (Footage by Leon Neal/Getty Images)

Ads for Elon Musk’s “Swasticar” Go Viral as Tesla Crumbles
==========================================================

Free market capitalism strikes again.

![Image 4: Noor Al-Sibai Avatar](https://futurism.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/avatar_user_151823_1741024562.jpg?quality=85&w=102&h=102&crop=1)

By[Noor Al-Sibai](https://futurism.com/authors/nooralsibai)

Published  Feb 27, 2025 9:15 AM EST

![Image 5: Hatred for Elon Musk seems to be everywhere one looks this week, from viral ads to Tesla's ever-plummeting stock value.](https://futurism.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/02/tesla-stocks-elon-musk-swasticar.jpg?quality=85&w=1152)

_Image: Everyone Hates Elon via Instagram / Valerie Plesch for The Washington Post via Getty / Futurism_

Palpable hatred for Elon Musk seems to be everywhere you look this week, from viral ads to Tesla’s plummeting stock value.

Across the pond in London Town, a group of anti-Musk crusaders operating under the handle “[Everyone Hates Elon](https://www.instagram.com/everyonehateselon_/)” have erected a bus stop ad that features the billionaire doing his infamous “[Sieg Heil](https://www.nytimes.com/2025/01/24/world/europe/elon-musk-roman-salute-nazi.html)” salute and calls Teslas “Swasticars,” both serving as allusions to the unelected political wrecker’s [increasingly far-right politics and activities](https://www.nbcnews.com/tech/elon-musk/elon-musk-boosting-far-right-politics-globe-rcna189505).

“Goes from 0 to 1939 in 3 seconds,” the ad’s copy reads — a reference to the year [Nazi Germany invaded Poland](https://www.dw.com/en/hitlers-germany-invaded-poland-85-years-ago/a-70094912), thus sparking off World War II.

> London Guerrilla Ad-fare: [#Tesla](https://twitter.com/hashtag/Tesla?src=hash&ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw) the [#Swasticar](https://twitter.com/hashtag/Swasticar?src=hash&ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw) … 
> 
> from 0 to 1939 in just 3 seconds [#Musk](https://twitter.com/hashtag/Musk?src=hash&ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw)[pic.twitter.com/y96FiQ5g1Z](https://t.co/y96FiQ5g1Z)
> 
> — Peter Speetjens (@PeterBeirut) [February 24, 2025](https://twitter.com/PeterBeirut/status/1894107083923931318?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw)

In the days since the guerrilla group behind the “Swasticar” ad posted videos of it on [Instagram](https://www.instagram.com/p/DGdKXnpoXHS/) and [TikTok](https://www.tiktok.com/@everyonehateselon/video/7474961006171540758?lang=en), their biting missive has been [viewed and shared millions of times](https://www.newsweek.com/anti-elon-musk-swasticar-advert-tiktok-2035950) — all while Tesla’s value spirals ever downward thanks in part to Musk’s wrecking ball approach at the [Department of Government Efficiency](https://futurism.com/doge-boy-website) (DOGE).

As [market summaries show](https://www.marketwatch.com/investing/stock/tsla), Tesla’s stock has crashed tremendously in recent days amid an [overall market drop](https://apnews.com/article/stocks-markets-rates-tariffs-china-86706b1215b5be59466c77f577ae888b) and [historically low sales numbers](https://www.cbsnews.com/news/elon-musk-tesla-sales-europe-drop-bucking-ev-trend-share-price/) in Europe. Though Donald Trump’s presidential win last November delivered a spike in value that drove Tesla stock up to an all-time high of $436 per share, it’s since plummeted, hitting $360 per share on February 20 and just under $291 by the close of markets on Wednesday.

As [_Business Insider_ reports](https://www.businessinsider.com/tesla-stock-sales-slide-elon-musk-doge-trump-electric-vehicles-2025-2), even finance bros that used to be in Tesla’s corner now seem convinced that Musk’s headlong foray into politics is harming his brand.

“The worry of [Wall Street] is that Musk dedicating so much time (even more than we expected) to DOGE takes away from his time at Tesla in such a crucial moment and year for the company,” [Tesla-stanning](https://www.teslarati.com/tesla-tsla-continues-soar-wedbush-price-target-up-2nd-time-since-trump-win/) Wedbush analyst Dan Ives wrote in an investor note viewed by _BI_.

In a [lengthy post on Musk’s social network](https://x.com/garyblack00/status/1893700442573705603), financial advisor and Tesla investor Gary Black admitted that he had been “wrongly bullish” on the EV company for years. Though he danced around the heart of the matter and refused to outright criticize the company’s CEO, the Future Fund managing partner said he hopes to “learn from [his] mistakes” when forecasting stock success, which seems like financespeak for throwing one’s hands up in the air.

By all accounts, Musk’s politicking has not only [harmed his business’ image](https://www.nytimes.com/2025/02/20/business/elon-musk-tesla-trump.html), but also hurt his bottom line — a sign, if there ever was one, that the [free market capitalism](https://robertreich.substack.com/p/elon-musks-grotesque-distortion-of) he and his cronies espouse may not always work in their favor.

Anti-Tesla Sentiment Goes International, Viral
==============================================

*    by [Tanya Gazdik](https://www.mediapost.com/publications/author/3041/tanya-gazdik/) , February 26, 2025 

![Image 9: Bus stop advert with GOES FROM 0 TO 1939 IN 3 SECONDS above a Tesla car and a man in the car holding one arm up and text below saying TESLA THE SWASTICAR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/media.mediapost.com/dam/cropped/2025/02/26/anti-elon-2_LxJfVJu.jpg)

Tesla sales continue to falter while the anti-Elon Musk sentiment continues to build.

“Tesla sales almost halved in Europe in January, the month of Donald Trump’s inauguration – quite possibly due to the far-right politics of founder Elon Musk, who is the president’s right-hand man,” [according to More About Advertising](https://www.moreaboutadvertising.com/2025/02/everyone-hates-elon-guerilla-campaign-condemns-the-swasticar/). “E-vehicle owners are likely to be a little more left-leaning, and sure enough Tesla sales were down 45% while the market as a whole grew by 34%.”

A group billing itself as Everyone Hates Elon is stoking the flames “with a guerrilla campaign in the U.K. and Germany that labels Tesla as The Swasticar. Musk’s support of far-right German party AfD and for alleged human trafficker Andrew Tate can’t have helped sales in Europe,” according to More About Advertising.

advertisement

[![Image 10: MPolitics-wi26-Advertising-640x480dbl.gif](https://cdn.broadstreetads.com/assets/5d4d04b4-5b07-42e4-85a4-87205fe47b0c.gif)](https://events.mediapost.com/event/politics-dc-2026/home "MPolitics-wi26-Advertising-640x480dbl.gif")

advertisement

“In Bethnal Green in East London, a poster has now emerged at a bus stop garnering significant online attention,” [according to _The Hollywood Reporter_](https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/news/general-news/elon-musk-poster-london-tesla-sales-drop-1236147614/). “‘Goes from 0 to 1939 in 3 seconds,’ the image says, with a picture of Musk in a Tesla below. The photo is taken from the moment Musk, also the founder of SpaceX, made what looked like a Nazi salute at Trump’s January inauguration rally, drawing criticism from all over the globe. The poster dubs Tesla ‘The Swasticar.’”

The fake ad received over 6 million views on TikTok after just a few days, [according to _Newsweek_](https://www.newsweek.com/anti-elon-musk-swasticar-advert-tiktok-2035950).

The Everyone Hates Elon group has a GoFundMe page where proceeds go to the costs of campaigning against Musk. The group claims to have plastered “Don’t buy a swasticar” stickers across hundreds of Teslas in London.

Billionaire-turned-Trump-henchman Musk continues in his role as head of the U.S. Department of Government Efficiency while remaining CEO of Tesla.

The anti-Musk sentiment also continues to ramp up in the U.S.

“In San Francisco, the intersection of Van Ness Avenue and O’Farrell Street is fast becoming the go-to hotspot for anti-Elon Musk resistance,” [according to SF Gate](https://www.sfgate.com/bayarea/article/sf-tesla-showroom-protest-elon-musk-20184983.php). “On Saturday, the busy junction that plays home to Tesla’s lone car dealership in the city saw its fourth substantial protest in eight days. More than 100 people gathered — some for their second protest of the week — to chant, wave signs, scare away potential customers and commiserate about the CEO’s power grab in the federal government.”

One sign suggests that drivers “Honk if you hate Elon.”

Some embarrassed Tesla owners worldwide are putting “I bought this before Elon went crazy” stickers onto their vehicles. In Norway, Kia is getting in on the joke with its own sticker asserting that former Tesla owners are switching to Kia with a similar sticker: “I bought this after Elon went crazy.”

The Collective Trying to Damage Elon Musk with Simple and Linear Graphics
=========================================================================

 9 months ago 

 - 

 Collater.al Contributors 

![Image 12: Close-up of a car with Tesla logo next to a sticker of Elon Musk wearing a Hitler moustache with the words DON'T BUY A SWASTICAR](https://www.collater.al/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Snapinsta.app_475538563_600691826180002_6603385620780183917_n_1080-819x1024.jpg)

In England, a [collective](https://www.instagram.com/everyonehateselon_/) called _**Everyone Hates Elon**_ has attracted significant attention with a provocative campaign against **Elon Musk** and **Tesla**. Posters put up in London—featuring a simple and linear design—read: _“From 0 to 1939 in three seconds. Tesla, the Swasticar,”_ linking Musk to Nazi symbols. The controversy gained traction on social media, with support from celebrities like Stephen King, highlighting the growing discontent towards the billionaire. But how can someone like Elon Musk, who has often thrived on negative publicity, actually be harmed? Let’s take a closer look at how _Everyone Hates Elon_ is trying to do it.

> Visualizza questo post su Instagram
> 
> 
> [Un post condiviso da Everyone Hates Elon (@everyonehateselon_)](https://www.instagram.com/p/DGqaV2DI0Gn/?utm_source=ig_embed&utm_campaign=loading)

The initiative by _Everyone Hates Elon_ was born in response to Musk’s support for Tommy Robinson, a far-right British activist currently in prison. The collective decided to target Tesla, viewing it as a symbol of Musk’s influence._«Buying one of his cars is like voting for him,_» the group stated.

![Image 13: A woman is taking a photo of a bus stop ad that reads GOES FROM 0 TO 1939 IN 3 SECONDS with an image of a Tesla car and the words TESLA THE SWASTICAR](https://www.collater.al/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Snapinsta.app_481502937_1339281053943748_8135445279337181096_n_1080-819x1024.jpg)
Criticism of Musk goes beyond his political stance: the billionaire is accused of exploiting workers, spreading reactionary ideas, and using X to amplify hate speech and misinformation. His ties to Donald Trump and his alleged gestures during the tycoon’s inauguration have further fueled protests against him.

![Image 15: A bus stop advertisement displays the text Elon Musk is a bellend, signed the UK.](https://www.collater.al/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Snapinsta.app_483024948_1201497748313091_1251271146311163880_n_1080-819x1024.jpg)
_Everyone Hates Elon_ isn’t just against Musk—it aims to send a broader message against the unchecked power of billionaires in politics and society. _«We’re tired of people like him who think they can influence our lives without any accountability,_» members of the collective say. With this campaign, the group seeks to demonstrate that opposition to Musk is growing and that more people are ready to challenge his negative impact on the world. Now, the question remains: will this campaign against the billionaire actually make a difference?

Tesla dubbed “Swasticar” in out-of-home actionist campaign
==========================================================

A range of OOH displays by activist groups have been criticising Elon Musk and his Tesla car brand, with slogans including “Goes from 0 to 1939 in 3 seconds”

![Image 10: A 50x50 small image, likely a logo, icon or avatar](https://www.signlink.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2024/09/Johnny_Enhanced_HEAD-scaled.jpg)

Jonathan Pert

March 3, 2025

UK activist group, Everyone Hates Elon, is behind the OOH campaign

*   [](https://www.facebook.com/sharer/sharer.php?u=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.signlink.co.uk%2Fnews%2Fout-of-home%2Ftesla-dubbed-swasticar-in-out-of-home-actionist-campaign%2F&t=Tesla%20dubbed%20%E2%80%9CSwasticar%E2%80%9D%20in%20out-of-home%20actionist%20campaign "Share on Facebook")
*   [](https://x.com/intent/tweet?text=Tesla%20dubbed%20%E2%80%9CSwasticar%E2%80%9D%20in%20out-of-home%20actionist%20campaign&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.signlink.co.uk%2Fnews%2Fout-of-home%2Ftesla-dubbed-swasticar-in-out-of-home-actionist-campaign%2F "Share on X")
*   [](https://www.linkedin.com/shareArticle?url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.signlink.co.uk%2Fnews%2Fout-of-home%2Ftesla-dubbed-swasticar-in-out-of-home-actionist-campaign%2F&title=Tesla%20dubbed%20%E2%80%9CSwasticar%E2%80%9D%20in%20out-of-home%20actionist%20campaign&summary=A%20range%20of%20OOH%20displays%20by%20activist%20groups%20have%20been%20criticising%20Elon%20Musk%20and%20his%20Tesla%20car%20brand%2C%20with%20slogans%20including%20%E2%80%9CGoes%20from%200%20to%201939%20in%203%20seconds%E2%80%9D&mini=true "Share on LinkedIn")
*   [](mailto:?subject=Tesla%20dubbed%20%E2%80%9CSwasticar%E2%80%9D%20in%20out-of-home%20actionist%20campaign&body=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.signlink.co.uk%2Fnews%2Fout-of-home%2Ftesla-dubbed-swasticar-in-out-of-home-actionist-campaign%2F "Send over email")

The actions of billionaire owner of Tesla and X (formerly Twitter), Elon Musk, have been likened to fascism in an out-of-home (OOH) project from a UK activist group.

During the inauguration celebrations of American president Donald Trump, Musk twice gave a one-armed salute akin to the ‘Sieg Heil’ salute of the Nazi Party.

Supporters later claimed that the gesture was a ‘Roman salute’, with Musk saying on his self-owned social media platform, X: “The 'everyone is Hitler' attack is sooo tired."

In response, an OOH poster mocking Musk and Tesla has appeared in Bethnal Green, East London, with the slogan: “Goes from 0 to 1939 in 3 seconds,” along with a picture of Musk saluting from the rally.

In the same billboard, Musk’s Tesla vehicles are dubbed “The Swasticar,” with people encouraged to stop purchasing the luxury electric vehicle brand.

The campaign is the work of a UK activist group called ‘Everyone Hates Elon’. A TikTok video the organisation posted of a man in high-vis clothing erecting the sign has so far garnered more than one million likes and nine million views.

Everyone Hates Elon also installed a sign on a London underground train, with the photo of Musk saluting alongside a graph representing Tesla’s falling stock price. A caption reads: “Hate doesn’t sell. Just ask Tesla.”

Between December 2024 and February 2025, the stock price of Tesla has fallen from a high of $479.86 (£379.39) to a low of $281.95 (£222.92), although this is still higher than the low of $142.05 (£110.08) reached in April of 2024.

The organisation has also reportedly stuck hundreds of stickers on Tesla cars across London that read: “Don’t buy a swasticar”.

![Image 11: Elon Musk salutes next to the words Heil Tesla projected on a Tesla factory](https://www.signlink.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/musk-1.jpg)

_Led by Donkeys also recently launched a campaign criticising Tesla and Musk_

Everyone Hates Elon has a fundraising page where proceeds go to the costs of campaigning against Musk. On the page, the group claims that Musk is promoting far-right politics in Europe. As of the date of publication, the campaign has raised over £14,200.

The group’s statement about the fundraiser reads: “Not happy with fuelling the far-right in the USA, Elon Musk is now doing the same in Europe.

“We can’t let the richest man in the world poison our politics. While nurses use food banks, his wealth grew by $200bn last year. Everyone Hates Elon is doing actions holding Elon to account. All proceeds will go directly towards the costs of our campaigning.”

The activist group, Led By Donkeys, launched a similar campaign last week, projecting an image of Musk giving the salute on the outside of the Tesla ‘Gigafactory’ in Berlin. An additional word has been projected next to the Tesla logo, so that it now reads: “Heil Tesla”.

An unverified video shared on X earlier this month also appears to show a Tesla totem sign in Birmingham edited to read: “Now Powered with Small D*ck Energy”.

=======================================================
