“Don’t buy a Swasticar” —this is what’s written on the stickers with which the activist group _Everyone Hates Elon_ has labeled Tesla cars on the streets of London. The action is part of _The People vs Elon_ campaign, which has already raised over £50,000 in support of anti-racist and anti-fascist initiatives.

Elsewhere, the reaction has been even more direct. In Portland, Oregon—a city famous not only for [Nike](https://author.edidomus.it/content/domusweb20/it/news/archive/2025/02/21/Nike) but also as one of the most important hubs of counterculture and dissent in the United States—someone spray-painted “NAZI” on Tesla cars. In Salem, also in Oregon, tensions escalated further: a Tesla dealership was targeted with gunfire and set on fire. Similar incidents have occurred in other parts of the U.S., from Colorado to California.

[Read also: All the ways Elon Musk made headlines this year](https://www.domusweb.it/en/news/gallery/2024/12/11/5-things-elon-musk-did-in-2024.html)

In other parts of the world, Tesla cars are often scratched with keys, and dealerships have been attacked with graffiti like “No Nazi.” Some Tesla owners themselves are distancing themselves from the brand with stickers reading, “When I bought this car, Elon was still normal” or “I bought it before Elon went crazy.”

![Image 14: Elon Musk with arm raised speaks from behind presidential podium with Seal of the President of the United States against blue and white backdrop of stars and stripes](https://www.domusweb.it/content/dam/domusweb/it/news/2025/02/21/cosa-sta-succedendo-a-tesla/domus-elon-musk-saluto-8.jpg.foto.rmedium.jpg)

Elon Musk at the inauguration ceremony of US President Donald Trump

The first major symbolic episode of this hostility was the attack on Tesla’s Gigafactory in Berlin, where the phrase “Heil Tesla” appeared on the building’s facade. A year earlier, the same factory had been hit by an arson attack. However, the recent escalation of hate seems to have a key date: January 20. During the inauguration that returned [Donald Trump](https://www.domusweb.it/it/dall-archivio/2024/11/06/Trump-tower-progetto-1983.html) to the White House, [Elon Musk](https://www.domusweb.it/it/notizie/gallery/2024/12/11/elon-musk-progetti-uomo-piu-ricco-storia-twitter-trump.html) greeted the crowd with a gesture that was interpreted worldwide as a double “Heil Hitler.” He tried to justify it as a simple “My heart goes to you,” but the incident fed into a growing perception of his alignment with far-right extremism. As Kurt Vonnegut wrote, _“we must be careful about what we pretend to be,”_ and in Musk’s case, his global image has rapidly turned into a meme of epic proportions.

![Image 15: Side of a white car with graffiti that reads FUCK - ELON in black spray paint](https://www.domusweb.it/content/dam/domusweb/it/news/2025/02/21/cosa-sta-succedendo-a-tesla/domus-tesla-musk-1.jpg.foto.rmedium.jpg)

Tesla: From Symbol of Progress to Divisive Icon
-----------------------------------------------

Elon Musk, often mistaken for an inventor (which he is not), built his career as an entrepreneur with companies like Hyperloop, The Boring Company, X (formerly Twitter), SpaceX, xAI, and even PayPal. But the name most associated with him is Tesla. Founded in 2003, Musk joined in 2004 with a $6.5 million investment, becoming CEO in 2008—the same year the first, legendary Roadster was launched. Two years later, Tesla went public on the Nasdaq.

![Image 16: A white Tesla Model 3 is parked on the street, vandalized with a red swastika spray-painted on its hood and windshield](https://www.domusweb.it/content/dam/domusweb/it/news/2025/02/21/cosa-sta-succedendo-a-tesla/domus-tesla-musk-6.jpeg.foto.rmedium.jpg)

Something has definitely flipped. Tesla, the brand that once didn’t need advertising, has become the Antichrist. And this is happening just as Chinese electric cars are becoming more competitive than ever. To seal this shift in perception, one of the most striking images circulating online today is from Portuguese illustrator Zez Vaz: a redesigned version of the famous Tiananmen Square photo, where the lone man standing in front of tanks has been replaced with a row of Cybertrucks. The message is clear: Tesla, once a symbol of the future, has become the emblem of an oppressive power crushing dissent.

Tesla and the Shift in Perception
---------------------------------

In the days following Musk’s gesture on Inauguration Day, memes began circulating online, distorting the Tesla Model S name into “Model SS”—a clear reference to the infamous Nazi _Schutzstaffel_. Paradoxically, the Third Reich produced one of the longest-lasting cars in history, the Volkswagen Beetle, and within Nazism, environmentalism was intertwined with racist ideology—Hitler, for example, was a vegetarian.

Something has definitely flipped. Tesla, the brand that once didn’t need advertising, has become the Antichrist. And this is happening just as Chinese electric cars are becoming more competitive than ever. To seal this shift in perception, one of the most striking images circulating online today is from Portuguese illustrator Zez Vaz: a redesigned version of the famous Tiananmen Square photo, where the lone man standing in front of tanks has been replaced with a row of Cybertrucks. The message is clear: Tesla, once a symbol of the future, has become the emblem of an oppressive power crushing dissent.

[Read also: Is Elon Musk's prefabricated mini-apartment the home of the future?](https://www.domusweb.it/en/news/2024/11/14/elon-musk-mini-apartment-boxabl.html)

The myth of Tesla as the car of optimism and progress now seems definitively buried.

10.title: Everyone Hates Elon - People vs Elon
10.description: Turning Elon's tweets into a weapon against the far right
10.content:
Stand against Elon

![Image 1: Woman takes a photo of a poster that says "goes from 0 to 1939 in 3 seconds - Tesla, the Swasticar"](https://peoplevselon.contentfiles.net/media/images/Screenshot_2025-03-14_at_12.45.54.2e16d0ba.fill-600x338.png)

**This is huge: our protests were just on national news as the reason that Tesla has lost $800 billion*.**

Let’s turn every single Elon Musk tweet into a weapon against him.

Pledge as little as 1p per tweet and we’ll turn small donations into small actions taking on the world’s richest man and pissing him off.

Make your pledge
----------------

Elon Musk tweets around 2,000 times a month. You can pledge as little as 1p every time he tweets, and choose to cap your regular donation.

[Give Once](https://www.gofundme.com/f/people-vs-elon?attribution_id=sl:aad3d7f4-7b34-4625-b481-d097ef0705ec&lang=en_GB&utm_campaign=man_sharesheet_dash&utm_medium=customer&utm_source=copy_link)

ADD YOUR SUPPORT

**We can’t let the richest man in the world poison our politics. While nurses use food banks, his wealth grew by $200 billion last year.**

Everyone Hates Elon set out to challenge his hate by pissing him off, one small action at a time.

We’ve plastered [‘don’t buy a swasticar’ stickers](https://www.instagram.com/novaramedia/reel/DFcwA4GoN4o/?hl=en-gb) on hundreds of Teslas, exposed Tesla customers’ hypocrisy by taking a [cardboard cutout](https://www.instagram.com/reel/DGL4wKuIhSl/) of Musk’s salute to their flagship London showroom, and created a [parody Tesla ‘Swasticar’ ad](https://www.tiktok.com/@peoplevselon/video/7474961006171540758) that went viral around the world.

**Tesla has lost $800bn since the start of the year. We need to keep up this momentum.**

We are building a movement against billionaires who think they can divide ordinary people . So we’ve got no money from rich tech bros - but we do have each other.

**Pledge 1p every time Elon tweets to fund new plans: from printing to transport to stickers - and for a secret new stunt** where ordinary members of the public can show how they really feel about Swasticars (you’ll be the first to be invited).

Thank you for your support.

 What happens to my donation? 
Your donations will support Everyone Hates Elon campaign actions - like [these](https://www.instagram.com/everyonehateselon_/). 100% of the proceeds will go towards producing and delivering actions.

 How much could this cost me? 
Musk tweets around 2,000 times per month. At 1p per tweet, that's £20 monthly - but you can set a cap so it never goes over e.g. £5, £10 or £25.

A group of “Everyone Hates Elon” protesters have smashed up a [Tesla](https://www.standard.co.uk/topic/tesla) car with sledgehammers to vent their anger at the world’s richest man. The social media campaign group auctioned off the opportunity for Londoners to “smash the utter f*** out of a Tesla” in order to send a message to the electric car company’s billionaire CEO [Elon Musk](https://www.standard.co.uk/topic/elon-musk). [](https://www.outbrain.com/what-is/default/en) The group said it made what it calls an art installation to “create a symbol of resistance to billionaire influence” and said it will donate any money made from the stunt to food banks. In an explainer on its website, Everyone Hates Elon wrote: “Tesla is the source of a lot of Musk's power and wealth, and he takes great pride in the brand being a global leader. “Recently stocks have been crashing and people across Europe have been boycotting the brand - it's sent Musk and even Trump into a panic. “This participatory art installation lets people express their frustration with wealth inequality safely and legally, while creating something that will ultimately benefit those in need as we’ll be auctioning it to raise money for food banks”. The vehicle, which was destined for the scrapyard, was donated by an anonymous donor and its battery will also be recycled, the protesters added. [Tesla](https://www.standard.co.uk/topic/tesla) sales have plunged in Europe and the US, as buyers continue to boycott the car maker following Musk’s support for far-right movements. Data released in March 2025 by the European Automobile Manufacturers’ Association suggests Tesla sales dropped more than 40 per cent in February 2025, compared to the same period in 2024. Musk has championed far-right parties and figures in Europe, including Germany’s AFD and [Tommy Robinson](https://www.standard.co.uk/topic/tommy-robinson), with analysts believing his politics have contributed to the drop in the company’s EV sales. ### Read More [![Image 4: What protests are taking place in London this weekend? How to activate a rapid-response fundraising campaign
=====================================================

07 Mar 2025[In-depth](https://www.civilsociety.co.uk/type/in-depth.html)

A spokesperson for the Everyone Hates Elon campaign offers insight into how to seize the moment for maximum impact.

![Image 4: Elon Musk wants to amplify hate in the UK with a Tweet about freeing Tommy Robinson](https://www.civilsociety.co.uk/static/781e310d-5320-42bb-aefe2f389c504fd7/article_img_detail_5ba532e110cf7bcee7b0d6e49c027c8b_4a7c7e45a350/People-v-Elon-Musk.jpg)

The People vs. Elon campaign poster

 Credit: People vs. Elon 

When Elon Musk did *that* salute at Donald Trump’s inauguration, I felt like I had to do something. But what can you do to take on the world’s richest man, who owns one of the world’s biggest social platforms?

People vs Elon was our response. The idea is simple: turn every Musk tweet into a weapon against the far right. Here’s how it works: supporters can pledge as little as 1p for every tweet Musk posts. He tweets around 2,000 times per month, so at 1p per tweet is £20 monthly – but donors can set an amount that it never goes over eg £5, £10 or £25. We then donate the funds raised to causes that represent everything he hates: trans people, refugees, and antiracist groups. Our partners include Everyday Racism, Hope not Hate, Rainbow Migration and Women for Refugee Women.

Anti-Musk poster campaign fuels the Musk/Tesla backlash
=======================================================

London's public transport network has become a canvas for unauthorised posters targeting Elon Musk
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

![Image 7: Gemma Gould](https://centralbylines.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2023/08/Gemma_Gould-150x150.jpg)by[Gemma Gould](https://centralbylines.co.uk/author/gemma-gould/)

[21-03-2025 12:24 - Updated On 24-03-2025 14:00](https://centralbylines.co.uk/politics/the-anti-musk-poster-campaign-in-london-a-growing-backlash/)

in[Politics](https://centralbylines.co.uk/category/politics/)

 Reading Time: 7 mins 

A A

A A Reset

[![Image 8: A Tesla advertisement at a bus stop boasts "0 to 1939 in 3 seconds," featuring a car and a man gesturing confidently.](https://centralbylines.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/My_mockup_2_from_Billboard_Mockup_Pack-750x536.jpg) A mockup of an @everyonehateselon poster used with permission.](https://centralbylines.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/My_mockup_2_from_Billboard_Mockup_Pack-scaled.jpg)

[Share on Bluesky](https://bsky.app/intent/compose?text=Anti-Musk%20poster%20campaign%20fuels%20the%20Musk%2FTesla%20backlash%20https%3A%2F%2Fcentralbylines.co.uk%2Fpolitics%2Fthe-anti-musk-poster-campaign-in-london-a-growing-backlash%2F)[](mailto:?subject=Anti-Musk%20poster%20campaign%20fuels%20the%20Musk%2FTesla%20backlash&body=https%3A%2F%2Fcentralbylines.co.uk%2Fpolitics%2Fthe-anti-musk-poster-campaign-in-london-a-growing-backlash%2F)[](https://api.whatsapp.com/send?text=Anti-Musk%20poster%20campaign%20fuels%20the%20Musk%2FTesla%20backlash%0Ahttps%3A%2F%2Fcentralbylines.co.uk%2Fpolitics%2Fthe-anti-musk-poster-campaign-in-london-a-growing-backlash%2F)[](https://www.linkedin.com/shareArticle?url=https%3A%2F%2Fcentralbylines.co.uk%2Fpolitics%2Fthe-anti-musk-poster-campaign-in-london-a-growing-backlash%2F&title=Anti-Musk%20poster%20campaign%20fuels%20the%20Musk%2FTesla%20backlash)[](https://reddit.com/submit?url=https%3A%2F%2Fcentralbylines.co.uk%2Fpolitics%2Fthe-anti-musk-poster-campaign-in-london-a-growing-backlash%2F&title=Anti-Musk%20poster%20campaign%20fuels%20the%20Musk%2FTesla%20backlash)[](https://www.facebook.com/sharer.php?u=https%3A%2F%2Fcentralbylines.co.uk%2Fpolitics%2Fthe-anti-musk-poster-campaign-in-london-a-growing-backlash%2F)[](https://twitter.com/intent/tweet?text=Anti-Musk%20poster%20campaign%20fuels%20the%20Musk%2FTesla%20backlash&url=https%3A%2F%2Fcentralbylines.co.uk%2Fpolitics%2Fthe-anti-musk-poster-campaign-in-london-a-growing-backlash%2F)

**In recent weeks, London’s public transport network has become a canvas for unauthorised posters targeting Elon Musk, the controversial CEO of Tesla, SpaceX and owner of the social media platform X (formerly Twitter). These posters, which have appeared on buses, bus stops and in Tube stations, employ provocative imagery and slogans to criticise Musk’s actions and affiliations.**

**Anti-Musk posters emerge in London**
--------------------------------------

The campaign against Musk gained significant attention with the appearance of a poster at a bus stop in Bethnal Green, East London. The poster depicted a Tesla vehicle branded as the “Swasticar,” accompanied by the slogan: “Goes from 0 to 1939 in 3 seconds.” This imagery alluded to Musk’s controversial gesture at Donald Trump’s inauguration rally, which many interpreted as [reminiscent of a Nazi salute](https://centralbylines.co.uk/politics/elon-musk-and-the-fascist-salute-controversy/).

Following this,[additional posters](https://www.instagram.com/p/DGdtFHpIgal/) surfaced across the city mocking the billionaire’s persona and political stance. [One such advert,](https://www.thelondoneconomic.com/news/searing-elons-musk-ad-appears-on-london-underground-390461/?utm_source=chatgpt.com) styled as a perfume promotion, featured the phrase “Elon’s Musk” with the tagline “Pour W*nkers”. Another poster at a London bus stop declared: “Elon Musk is a bellend, signed the UK.”

The organisation ‘[Everyone Hates Elon](https://www.instagram.com/everyonehateselon_/?hl=en)‘ has claimed responsibility for these guerrilla adverts. Their campaign aims to highlight and protest against Musk’s recent political actions and affiliations, particularly his support for [far-right movements](https://www.lemonde.fr/en/europe/article/2025/01/10/musk-doubles-down-on-support-for-german-far-right-leader_6736883_143.html) in Europe and his involvement with President Donald Trump. The group has also distributed stickers reading “Don’t buy a Swasticar,” which have been spotted [on Tesla vehicles](https://www.instagram.com/p/DFcydx3I8sr/?utm_source=ig_embed&utm_campaign=loading) throughout London.

**Official response “unauthorised”**
------------------------------------

Transport for London (TfL) has acknowledged the presence of these unauthorised posters and stated that they are working to remove them from the transport network. A [TfL spokesperson commented](https://www.thelondoneconomic.com/news/tfl-releases-statement-on-anti-elon-musk-posters-appearing-around-london-390476/?utm_source=chatgpt.com): “These adverts are not authorised by TfL or our advertising partner. We have instructed our contractor to remove any found on our network.”

The campaign has sparked discussions among the public, with some expressing support for the messages conveyed, while others debate the appropriateness of the methods used. Social media platforms have seen a surge in shares and comments regarding the posters, reflecting a wide range of opinions.

**Anti-Musk ‘Tesla Takedown’ movement in the US**
-------------------------------------------------

The anti-Musk movement in London is part of a larger wave of discontent against the billionaire. In the United States, a similar initiative known as ‘[Tesla Takedown](https://edition.cnn.com/2025/03/01/business/tesla-takedown-musk-doge/index.html)‘ has been gaining traction. This campaign involves protests outside Tesla showrooms, coordinated social media activism and calls for boycotts against the brand. Demonstrators in [cities like New York](https://www.reuters.com/world/us/nine-arrested-new-york-tesla-dealership-anti-musk-protests-break-out-2025-03-02/), Los Angeles, and Chicago have staged events criticising Musk’s business practices, his management of X, and his alignment with controversial political figures and ideology.

The growing resistance to Musk highlights broader concerns about the power and influence of billionaire tech moguls. While some view Musk as a visionary entrepreneur, others see him as emblematic of unchecked corporate influence and political interference. The emergence of campaigns like ‘Everyone Hates Elon’ and ‘Tesla Takedown’ suggests that public sentiment is shifting, with increasing scrutiny placed on business leaders who engage in political and social debates.

**Impact on Tesla’s reputation and sales**
------------------------------------------

The backlash against Musk has had tangible effects on Tesla’s market performance, particularly in Europe. Reports indicate that Tesla [sales have almost halved](https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2025/feb/25/tesla-sales-europe-elon-musk-donald-trump-afd) in Europe at the start of 2025, following Musk’s controversial actions and affiliations. This decline suggests that the public’s perception of Musk is influencing consumer behaviour, potentially impacting the company’s profitability in the region.

Additionally, industry analysts have pointed out that the growing association between Musk’s political stance and Tesla’s brand image could deter potential customers who prefer to distance themselves from polarising figures. [Some analysts believe](https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2025/mar/08/major-brand-worries-just-how-toxic-is-elon-musk-for-tesla) this could lead to long-term damage for the company if Musk continues to engage in political debates rather than focusing on the innovation and performance of his products.

[![Image 9: Ink drawing of Elon Musk, a man in a suit, at a podium with an X logo on it and X logos on black in the background, throwing a straight arm salute](https://centralbylines.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2025/02/WhatsApp-Image-2025-02-05-at-10.24.22-1100x570.jpeg)](https://centralbylines.co.uk/politics/elon-musk-and-the-fascist-salute-controversy/)

[News](https://centralbylines.co.uk/category/news/)

### [Elon Musk and the fascist salute controversy](https://centralbylines.co.uk/politics/elon-musk-and-the-fascist-salute-controversy/)

by[Gemma Gould](https://centralbylines.co.uk/author/gemma-gould/)

[5 February 2025](https://centralbylines.co.uk/politics/elon-musk-and-the-fascist-salute-controversy/)

**The role of social media in shaping public opinion**
------------------------------------------------------

Historically, tech moguls such as Steve Jobs and Bill Gates were viewed as visionary figures whose companies were synonymous with innovation and progress. However, the rise of social media has made business leaders more accessible to public scrutiny, with their political affiliations, personal statements and business practices facing greater examination.

The rapid spread of the anti-Musk posters has been facilitated by social media, where images and discussions about the campaign have gone viral. Hashtags such as #Swasticar, #BoycottTesla, and #MuskMeltdown have trended on platforms like X, Instagram and TikTok. The influence of social media in mobilising public opinion has been a significant factor in the campaign’s reach, enabling it to extend far beyond London.

The criticism is also being voiced through crowdsourcing platforms, where people express their frustrations through campaigns like ‘[People Versus Elon](https://peoplevselon.co.uk/)‘_,_ a site aimed at raising money for five organisations every time Musk tweets. As the scrutiny intensifies, it raises an important question: will Musk’s political affiliations continue to overshadow his business ventures or can he weather the storm of public opposition?

The shifting tide of public opinion, amplified by social media and grassroots activism, might ultimately shape the trajectory of Musk’s empire. Whether this marks the beginning of a lasting reputational shift remains to be seen.

The provocative nature of the posters has caught the attention of high-profile individuals. Notably, [celebrated author Stephen King](https://bsky.app/profile/stephenking.bsky.social/post/3liz373mszc2g) reposted an image of the poster

**Musk facing a considerable challenge?**
-----------------------------------------

The unauthorised anti-Musk posters appearing across London reflect a growing public sentiment against the billionaire’s recent actions and affiliations. The involvement of high-profile celebrities in sharing these posters has further amplified the discourse, highlighting the complex relationship between public figures, corporate actions and societal values.

With a parallel movement unfolding in the United States, Musk’s public perception appears to be at a critical juncture, where consumer and activist actions could shape the future of his business empire. Whether this marks the beginning of a significant reputational shift for Musk or simply a temporary wave of criticism remains to be seen. However, the response to these campaigns suggests that the public’s tolerance for billionaire influence in politics and social issues is facing a considerable challenge.

19.title: Venetians plan to march in the streets, swim in the canals to disrupt Jeff Bezos's wedding
19.description: Activists are doing whatever they can to disrupt Amazon founder Jeff Bezos's lavish nuptials in Venice, an Italian city protesters accuse of prioritizing the desires of wealthy tourists over the needs of its own residents.
19.content:
[As It Happens](https://www.cbc.ca/radio/asithappens)

Activists are doing whatever they can to disrupt Amazon founder Jeff Bezos's lavish nuptials in Venice, an Italian city protesters accuse of prioritizing the desires of wealthy tourists over the needs of its own residents.

While some Venetians welcome the lavish party, others see it as a symbol of inequality and over-tourism
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

![Image 1: A 38x38 small image, likely a logo, icon or avatar](https://i.cbc.ca/ais/1.6482181,1659119016000/full/max/0/default.jpg?im=Crop%2Crect%3D%281697%2C64%2C2504%2C2504%29%3BResize%3D114)

[Sheena Goodyear](https://www.cbc.ca/radio/author/sheena-goodyear-1.3631841) · CBC Radio

· Posted: Jun 23, 2025 6:04 PM EDT | Last Updated: June 24

![Image 2: Text to Speech Icon](https://www.cbc.ca/a/assets/texttospeech.svg)

Listen to this article

Estimated 6 minutes

The audio version of this article is generated by AI-based technology. Mispronunciations can occur. We are working with our partners to continually review and improve the results.

![Image 3: A bald man in a tuxedo poses next to a woman with long brown hair and a white gown.](https://i.cbc.ca/ais/1.7568841,1750712325000/full/max/0/default.jpg?im=Crop%2Crect%3D%280%2C85%2C5786%2C3254%29%3B)

Amazon founder Jeff Bezos, right, will marry journalist Lauren Sanchez, left, in a lavish, three-day wedding extravaganza in Venice.(Danny Moloshok/Reuters)

_**Update:** After this story published, [Reuters reported](https://www.reuters.com/business/media-telecom/bezos-venice-wedding-party-moved-isolated-area-security-concerns-2025-06-24/)that Jeff Bozos and Lauren Sanchez have decided to move their wedding party at Venice's Scuola Grande della Misericordia, where protests have been planned, to a more isolated and less accessible venue.Tommaso Cacciari, a leader of the No Space for Bezos protest group, called the move "a great victory for us."_

* * *

When the world's third richest man ties the knot in Venice this week, Federica Toninello plans to be just outside, having a swim in the canal.

Toninello is one of hundreds of protesters who are doing whatever they can to disrupt Amazon founder Jeff Bezos's lavish nuptials in Venice, an Italian city that activists say prioritizes the desires of wealthy tourists over the needs of its own residents.

As about 200 high-profile guests arrive in Venice, booking up huge swaths of luxury hotel rooms and water taxis, the demonstrators intend to block the streets and the waterways near the purported wedding venue.

"We are going put our bodies in the canals of Venice," Toninello told _As It Happens_ host Nil Kӧksal. "There are going to also be some boats. Whatever can float, we are going to use it."

**Bezos 'represents the future that we don't want'**
----------------------------------------------------

Bezos, 61, will wed former news anchor Lauren Sanchez, 55, this week after getting engaged in 2023.

The couple have not publicly released any details about the event, but local media outlets report there will be three days of festivities across the city, likely between June 26-28.

[The New York Times](https://www.nytimes.com/2025/06/20/style/jeff-bezos-lauren-sanchez-wedding.html), citing unconfirmed reports in Italian newspapers, identifies likely wedding event locations as Lido beach, where the Venice Film Festival is held; the entire island of San Giorgio, which is usually a public space; and the Scuola Grande della Misericordia, a restored Renaissance building and event space.

The latter is where activists believe the pair will say their vows — and that's where Toninello plans to make her splash, literally.

![Image 4: An aerial shot shows a few dozen people standing around a massive banner, unfurled and laid out on the ground. It's white with a picture of a bald man laughing, and the all-caps words: IF YOU CAN RENT VENICE FOR YOUR WEDDING YOU CAN PAY MORE TAX](https://i.cbc.ca/ais/1.7568849,1750712527000/full/max/0/default.jpg?im=Crop%2Crect%3D%280%2C0%2C5500%2C3614%29%3B)

A large anti-Bezos banner lies on the ground, placed by Greenpeace Italy activists and U.K. activist group Everyone Hates Elon, in Venice's St. Mark's Square, on June 23.(Yara Nardi/Reuters)

While Venice's mayor and some business owners have lauded the wedding as a source of income for the city, other Venetians are making it clear the couple are not welcome by unfurling massive banners in public areas and plastering the city with anti-Bezos posters.

Toninello is with the protest group No Space for Bezos, a collaboration of about a dozen Venetian organizations including housing advocates, anti-cruise ship campaigners and student activists.

The group's name is reference to Bezos's space technology company, Blue Origin, which recently launched a rocket with an all-female crew that included the bride-to-be.

![Image 5: People stand on an arched stone bridge unfurling a hand-painted banner with a rocket ship and big blue bubble letters that read: "No Space for Bezos!"](https://i.cbc.ca/ais/1.7568857,1750712618000/full/max/0/default.jpg?im=Crop%2Crect%3D%280%2C0%2C6000%2C4000%29%3B)

Protesters display a banner reading 'No Space for Bezos!' on the Rialto Bridge in Venice on June 13.(Manuel Silvestri/Reuters)

Toninello says the group's main goal is to draw attention to the effects of over-tourism in Venice, which she says has driven up housing costs and forced Venetian residents to pack up and leave.

They are calling on the government to invest in education, environmental protections and affordable housing to rebuild the dwindling local population.

"Tourism is not something that brings richness to the people. It's something that brings richness only to few people, and most of the time these people also do not live in Venice," Toninello said.

But she says they are also protesting Bezos, himself. She accused the billionaire of paying less than his fair share in taxes, and getting rich off the backs of the working poor.

"He represents the future that we don't want to live in," she said.

Bezos did not respond to a request for comment.

Ahead of the wedding, he made a charitable donation to Corila, a Venetian environmental research association, through his philanthropic organization, the Bezos Earth Fund

Corila wouldn't say how much Bezos was donating, but noted contacts began in April, well before the protests started.

**Businesses, politicians welcome the couple**
----------------------------------------------

The environmental group Greenpeace is also protesting the wedding.

Activists from Greenpeace Italy and U.K. group "Everyone Hates Elon" — referring to Tesla owner and former U.S. President Donald Trump ally, Elon Musk —unfolded a giant banner in central St. Mark's Square featuring a picture of Bezos laughing and a sign reading: "If you can rent Venice for your wedding, you can pay more tax."

"The problem is not the wedding, the problem is the system," Simona Abbate, one of the protesters, told Reuters. "We think that one big billionaire can't rent a city for his pleasure."

![Image 6: A bald man in glasses stands with his arms folded in front of a store building with the words "E. Rosa Salva" above the door in a cursive font.](https://i.cbc.ca/ais/1.7568873,1750713134000/full/max/0/default.jpg?im=Crop%2Crect%3D%280%2C0%2C8640%2C5760%29%3B)

Pastry shop owner Antonio Rosa Salva says Bezos and Sanchez have ordered Venetian specialties from his shop for their wedding.(Luca Bruno/The Associated Press)

But not everyone is opposed to the multimillion-dollar extravaganza.

Antonio Rosa Salva, whose pastry business is one of several local vendors supplying the wedding, said events like this bring "quality tourism" to the city.

"I don't see how an event with 200 people can create disruption," Salva said. "It's responsible tourism. It's prestigious that a couple like this, who can go anywhere in the world, are getting married in the city."

Regional governor Luca Zaia said the wedding will bring an economic windfall to local businesses, including the motor boats and gondolas that operate its myriad canals. He said the celebrations were expected to cost 20-30 million euros ($31-$47 million Cdn).

*   [Amazon starts closing Quebec warehouses as union president calls for boycott](https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/montreal/amazon-union-boycott-1.7454649)

*   [Amazon launches first batch of Kuiper internet satellites to compete with SpaceX's Starlink](https://www.cbc.ca/news/science/amazon-kuiper-satellite-constellation-1.7521528)

Venice Mayor Luigi Brugnaro lambasted the protesters while addressing reporters in Venice on Friday,[according to CNN](https://www.cnn.com/2025/06/17/travel/jeff-bezos-wedding-protests-divide-venice).

"We will have to apologize to Bezos," the mayor said. "I am ashamed of those who behave like this. I hope that Bezos comes anyway. Not all Venetians think like these protesters."

Toninello balked at the mayor's comments.

"The one that should be ashamed is him," she said. "The way the city is right now, it's because of him."

* * *

_With files from Reuters and The Associated Press. Interview with Federica Toninello produced by Chris Harbord_

Campaigners against [Elon Musk](https://bylinetimes.com/2024/08/12/leading-labour-mp-brands-twitter-owner-elon-musk-a-dangerous-narcissist-as-she-calls-for-clampdown-on-online-hate/) are inviting Londoners to smash up a Tesla in the latest of a series of protests and artistic stunts against the Trump-supporting billionaire that are spreading across the UK.

Titled ‘London vs Musk’, the art piece is to be put on by Everyone Hates Elon, the group behind satirical posters referring to Teslas as “Swasticars” which have appeared across London.

The event is billed as an opportunity for “Londoners to safely and legally smash up a Tesla to vent their rage at Elon Musk, the far-right and billionaires”, will see a second-hand Tesla which was set to be scrapped, smashed and auctioned to raise money for foodbanks this Saturday.

Electric vehicle producer Tesla has been targeted by activists due to its far-right owner’s interference in British politics

Josiah Mortimer

“There are more billionaires than ever before and there are more food banks than ever before. These things are obviously connected,” said an Everyone Hates Elon spokesperson.

Tesla owners who feel betrayed by Musk’s recent actions will be given priority access to smash the Tesla, the group said.

The Tesla brand has suffered considerable damage since Musk joined Trump’s administration as the head of the Department of Government Efficiency. Tesla stock has fallen by 38% since 02 January of this year.

![Image 19: Year to date graph shows the current stock price is 233.29 USD, which is 145.99 USD less than its value at the beginning of the year](https://bylinetimes.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/image-1.png)
According to the _Financial Times_, Tesla has just experienced its worst quarter since 2022. The company delivered 336,681 vehicles between January and March, this is 13 per cent fewer than a year earlier and well below the 390,000 expected by analysts.

Other actions as part of the recent wave of anti-Tesla protests have included [Just Stop Oil](https://bylinetimes.com/2024/08/13/just-stop-oils-whole-truth-five-to-appeal-years-long-sentences-after-sun-journalist-exposed-m25-disruption-plans/) vandalising a Tesla robot by pouring liquid latex over it and an international day of action in which [protesters](https://bylinetimes.com/2024/09/10/human-rights-group-demands-review-into-policing-of-unfairly-criminalised-gold-mine-protestors/) picketed Tesla showrooms in London, Berlin, Paris and several US cities.

[![Image 21: Elon Musk is seen in profile with his hands clasped together in front of his face, looking thoughtful or concerned](https://bylinetimes.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/01/musk-x.png)](https://bylinetimes.com/2025/01/27/elon-musk-grooming-gangs-uk/)

21.title: Massive Photo of Trump and Epstein Unfurled Outside Windsor Castle
21.description: Activists behind the action at the UK royal residence said they want to “make sure Epstein haunts him everywhere he goes.”
21.content:
[News](https://hyperallergic.com/tag/news/)
Activists behind the action at the UK royal residence said they want to “make sure Epstein haunts him everywhere he goes.”

[![Image 1: Maya Pontone](https://hyperallergic.com/content/images/size/w160/2025/11/cropped-img_8942-scaled-1-d-blank-r-g-s-500.jpg)](https://hyperallergic.com/author/maya-pontone/)

![Image 2: Massive Photo of Trump and Epstein Unfurled Outside Windsor Castle](https://hyperallergic.com/content/images/size/w1200/hyperallergic-newspack-s3-amazonaws-com/uploads/2025/09/trump-windsor.jpg)

Activists unfurl a large photo of US President Donald Trump posing with Jeffrey Epstein outside Windsor Castle on September 15. (photo by Everone Hates Elon/AFP via Getty Images)

Activists are determined to spoil Donald Trump’s state visit to the United Kingdom this week — one Jeffrey Epstein photo at a time.

Less than 24 hours ahead of his arrival at Windsor Castle, a supersized photo of the president with the convicted sexual predator was unveiled on the tree-lined property outside the royal residence yesterday, September 15. The massive banner display, which has since been removed, was carried out by the UK-based anti-billionaire collective [Everyone Hates Elon](https://www.instagram.com/everyonehateselon_/?ref=hyperallergic.com) as part of a crowd-funded campaign to plaster the notorious image of Trump and Epstein “all over the UK” in time for his historic state visit.

"[This image is] the last thing Trump wants the world to see," reads a description in the [online fundraiser](https://www.crowdfunder.co.uk/p/trump-uk-visit-epstein?ref=hyperallergic.com), which has so far garnered at least £32,016 (~$43,729) from hundreds of supporters. “So let's put it everywhere he goes and make sure the media can't avoid it - it'll be the defining image of the state visit he's so looking forward to."

This month, the group also installed [unofficial bus stop ads](https://www.instagram.com/p/DOdpD3hiC4M/?ref=hyperallergic.com)[by the US Embassy in London](https://www.instagram.com/p/DOJpB1yCF4A/?ref=hyperallergic.com), [spoof commemorative dishware](https://www.instagram.com/p/DOlZLdeiFU-/?ref=hyperallergic.com) in the Windsor Castle Gift Shop, and a [parody memorial plaque](https://www.instagram.com/p/DOY1jODiBU4/?ref=hyperallergic.com) on a bench on Trump’s Aberdeen golf course in Scotland.

0:00

/0:00

The anti-billionaire collective affixing a [parody memorial plaque to Epstein](https://www.instagram.com/p/DOY1jODiBU4/?ref=hyperallergic.com) on a bench on Trump’s Aberdeen golf course. (reel via @everyonehateselon_ on [Instagram](https://www.instagram.com/reel/DOYXYaziK7S/?utm_source=ig_web_copy_link&igsh=MzRlODBiNWFlZA==))

![Image 3](https://hyperallergic.com/massive-photo-of-trump-and-epstein-unfurled-outside-windsor-castle/data-kg-custom-thumbnail=https://g.hyperallergic.com/content/images/videos-files-wordpress-com/8banIZ1S/24ab9e7244474dabbeaf4c9f51bdea40_mp4_hd-original.jpg)
The trolling comes amid intensifying scrutiny over the president’s relationship with Epstein, which was exacerbated last week when the United States House Oversight Committee [released a vulgar note](https://hyperallergic.com/newly-released-jeffrey-epstein-birthday-drawings-paint-a-disturbing-picture/) supposedly penned by Trump that was part of a salacious birthday album gifted to the disgraced financier by his former assistant and accomplice Ghislaine Maxwell. The book contained hundreds of crude poems, drawings, photos, and messages bearing the alleged signatures of Epstein’s close friends, including Museum of Modern Art Trustee Leon Black and Wexner Center for the Arts financier Leslie Wexner.

Subscribe to Hyperallergic
--------------------------

Get the free version of our newsletter. Unsubscribe anytime.

“Trump’s supporters are tearing themselves apart over the Epstein files. Now he’s hoping to escape it all to have tea with the King,” a spokesperson for Everyone Hates Elon said in a press statement.

Aimed at deepening US relations with one of the country’s closest allies, Trump’s trip is [expected to involve copious amounts of grandeur](https://abcnews.go.com/Politics/trump-heads-uk-historic-2nd-state-visit/story?id=125584310&ref=hyperallergic.com) and flattery on behalf of the UK government, much like his first state visit in 2019.

_Hyperallergic_ has reached out to the Windsor Castle press office for comment.

![Image 4: Souvenir plates displayed on a shelf include one showing Donald Trump and Jeffrey Epstein with text that reads, A Special Relations[hip]](https://hyperallergic.com/content/images/hyperallergic-newspack-s3-amazonaws-com/uploads/2025/09/windsor-gift.jpg)

A satirical commemorative plate featuring Jeffrey Epstein and US President Donald Trump is seen among souvenirs in a gift shop in Windsor, England. (photo by Leon Neal/Getty Images)

The spokesperson for Everyone Hates Elon said that the collective intends “to make sure Epstein haunts him everywhere he goes.”

Earlier this summer, the group was partially responsible for a [massive banner in Venice targeting Amazon billionaire Jeff Bezos's opulent destination wedding plans](https://hyperallergic.com/venice-climate-activists-have-a-blunt-message-for-jeff-bezos/). The historic canal-lined city has been increasingly plagued by rising sea levels from climate change.

“There’s no way we’re letting [Trump] use our country to polish his image,” the spokesperson for Everyone Hates Elon said.

For their next action, the group is [potentially planning to parade](https://www.instagram.com/p/DOWXwwJCJa7/?fbclid=IwZXh0bgNhZW0CMTAAYnJpZBExRXg2bm9ZMXQ0VnU5bjZ3QwEeEirmIhIwnWWemeMsr_wcOHCcxVFRGDS6rm1vPW7jQVhTpZF1JHplDwI6Cvc_aem_PfWeNn5jprHZNFFcKw2aGA&ref=hyperallergic.com) the photo of Trump and Epstein with an ad van. But as far as details for that plan go, a group member simply told _Hyperallergic_ to “keep your eyes peeled.”

Why do fake Elon Musk ads keep appearing around London and on the Tube?
=======================================================================

The satirical posters are designed to take a swipe at multi-billionaire Tesla owner and world’s richest man Elon Musk


-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

[Alexander Butler](https://www.independent.co.uk/author/alexander-butler)

Sunday 16 March 2025 11:45 GMT

[Comments](https://www.independent.co.uk/news/uk/home-news/musk-fake-ads-london-tube-b2716053.html#comments-area)

“[Tesla](https://www.independent.co.uk/topic/tesla): The Swasticar”, reads a poster at a bus stop [opposite Sadler’s Well Theatre](https://www.independent.co.uk/tv/news/elon-musk-tesla-just-stop-oil-protest-b2714698.html). “Autopilot for your car. Autocrat for your country.”

First appearing around [Clerkenwell](https://www.independent.co.uk/topic/clerkenwell) in February, [London](https://www.independent.co.uk/topic/london) has since been plastered with guerrilla advertisements [comparing Elon Musk to a Nazi](https://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/americas/tesla-sales-slump-vandalism-dealership-musk-b2715032.html) over recent weeks.

It was a satirical swipe at the [multi-billionaire Tesla owner](https://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/americas/us-politics/trump-buy-tesla-musk-doge-b2712762.html) and world’s richest man. “We are holding Elon to account,” the group behind the poster said.

![Image 5: Posters taking a swipe at Elon Musk have appeared across London over recent weeks](https://static.independent.co.uk/2025/03/13/9/34/Everyone-Hates-Elon-Protest-Group-Continue-Their-Guerilla-Campaign-Against-Trumps-Favourite-Tech-Bro.jpeg)

open image in gallery

Posters taking a swipe at Elon Musk have appeared across London over recent weeks (Getty Images)

“Not happy with fuelling the far-right in the [USA](https://www.independent.co.uk/topic/usa), Elon Musk is now doing the same in [Europe](https://www.independent.co.uk/topic/europe). We can’t let the richest man in the world poison our politics,” it said.

Since then, copy-cat campaign groups have taken to erecting larger-scale billboard-style posters across other parts of the capital.

Here, _The Independent_ takes a look at who is behind the campaigns and why they are appearing across London.

![Image 6: The satirical posters appeared in Clerkenwell in February and have since spread across London](https://static.independent.co.uk/2025/03/14/11/42/SEI243609339-(1).jpeg)

open image in gallery

The satirical posters appeared in Clerkenwell in February and have since spread across London (Everybody Hates Elon)

Who is behind the campaigns?
----------------------------

Though it is not clear who the individuals are behind the groups, Everybody Hates Elon has vowed to “build a movement against billionaires” who “seek to divide ordinary people”.

“Everyone Hates Elon is doing actions holding Elon to account. All proceeds will go directly towards the costs of our campaigning,” the group said on its gofundme page.

Overthrow Musk said it was founded to “fight the oligarchs” and “defend democracy”, with their political stunts cropping up in Tottenham, Walthamstow and St Albans.

![Image 7: A billboard-style advert popped up in Walthamstow this week](https://static.independent.co.uk/2025/03/14/14/23/Gl6BzPPXEAAKKfz.jpeg)

open image in gallery

A billboard-style advert popped up in Walthamstow this week (Overthrow Musk)

Everybody Hates Elon was the first group reported to have erected the posters, which appeared in February.

A week later, the volunteer-led campaign group put up a series of fake advertisements on the London Underground comparing Musk to a Nazi.

It showed Musk appearing to give a Nazi salute next to Tesla’s dwindling share prices with the title: “Hate doesn’t sell. Just ask Tesla”.

A different poster showed an image of a fake “Elon’s Musk” swastika perfume bottle with the caption “Elon’s Musk, Parfum de 1939”.

![Image 8: A mock film advertisement for The Fast and Führer showing a Doge plated Telsa Model S next to the caption Heil Tesla was also put up in Tottenham](https://static.independent.co.uk/2025/03/14/14/35/Gl3JIFVbYAQKuWc.jpeg)

open image in gallery

A mock film advertisement for The Fast and Führer showing a Doge plated Telsa Model S next to the caption Heil Tesla was also put up in Tottenham (Overthrow Musk)

In Walthamstow, a billboard-style poster designed by a separate group Overthrow Musk showed an image of Musk with the words: “Buying a Tesla? You may be in for a Nazi surprise?”.

A mock film advertisement for “The Fast and Führer” showing a “Doge” plated Telsa Model S next to the caption “Heil Tesla” was also put up in Tottenham.

It had a fake PG warning reading: “Parental guidance. Tesla’s CEO is a far-right activist. Don’t give him your money.”

Why are they appearing?
-----------------------

Elon Musk was accused of giving what appeared to be a Nazi “salute” during a Trump inauguration rally in January. In response he said on X: “Frankly, they need better dirty tricks. [The “everyone is Hitler” attack is so tired.”](https://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/americas/us-politics/elon-musk-salute-trump-inauguration-b2683095.html)

Musk has made a number of high-profile attacks against Sir Keir Starmer and the Labour government, while throwing support behind right-wing party Reform.

![Image 9: Musk’s controversial salute at Trump’s inauguration parade](https://static.independent.co.uk/2025/01/21/08/elon-musk-heil-salute-far-right.jpg)

open image in gallery

Musk’s controversial salute at Trump’s inauguration parade (Getty Images)

In a slew of attacks in January, he accused the prime minister of being “complicit” in the [crimes carried out by UK grooming gangs](https://www.independent.co.uk/news/uk/politics/grooming-gangs-lisa-nandy-elon-musk-b2681392.html).

It also emerged that Musk had discussed how best to remove from office before the next UK general election.

_The Financial Times_ reported he was in talks with right-wing allies on how he could best destabilise the Labour government beyond his aggressive social media attacks on the PM.

The SpaceX and Tesla owner also took aim at Germany ahead of federal elections in February, endorsing and [promoting the far-right AfD](https://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/europe/elon-musk-afd-germany-election-b2702851.html), which came second in the polls.

Dan, who designs posters for Overthrow Musk, and only gave his first name, told _The Independent_: “Musk is an oligarch co-president. He is a very dangerous man and his Nazi salute and support for far-right European parties show this.

“But his weak spot is Tesla. His wealth is tied up in it. Reducing Tesla’s sales reduces his power. We are trying to make the link between Tesla and Musk more obvious.

What has the response been?
---------------------------

A Transport for London spokesperson said the posters were not authorised by the network, “and we have instructed our teams and contractors to remove any that are found on our network."

'Everyone Hates Elon' Campaign Targets Billionaire Jim Ratcliffe
================================================================

MANCHESTER, ENGLAND - NOVEMBER 10: A billboard poster by activist group 'Everyone Hates Elon depicts Sir Jim Ratcliffe and stating "If you can buy Manchester United you can pay more tax" on November 10, 2025 in Manchester, England. Sir Jim Ratcliffe, Manchester United co-owner and CEO of INEOS chemicals group, appears in this edition of a campaign against billionaires by activist group 'Everyone Hates Elon,' which has installed a series of posters and public artworks critical of Elon Musk and other business and political figures around the UK. Sledgehammer-wielding Musk critics smash up Tesla in London art project
=======================================================================

This article is more than 8 months old

Campaign group Everyone Hates Elon organised protest with car bound for scrapheap ‘to create debate about wealth inequality’

[Kate McCusker](https://www.theguardian.com/profile/kate-mccusker)

Thu 10 Apr 2025 20.32 BSTLast modified on Fri 11 Apr 2025 05.29 BST

[Share](mailto:?subject=Sledgehammer-wieldingMuskcriticssmashupTeslainLondonartproject&body=https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2025/apr/10/sledgehammer-wielding-musk-critics-smash-up-tesla-in-london-art-project?CMP=share_btn_url)

Protective helmets were donned and sledgehammers wielded as [Elon Musk](https://www.theguardian.com/technology/elon-musk) critics vented their frustration at the Tesla boss and billionaire by smashing up a disused Tesla bound for the scrapheap.

The public art project was organised by the social media campaign group Everyone Hates Elon. A 2014 [Tesla](https://www.theguardian.com/technology/tesla) Model S was provided by an anonymous donor “to create a debate about wealth inequality”, a spokesperson for the group said.

The participants gathered at Hardess Studios in south [London](https://www.theguardian.com/uk/london) on Thursday to take it in turns to swing at the car with sledgehammers and baseball bats. The destroyed electric vehicle, which retails for about £14,000, will be auctioned in the next few weeks, with all proceeds going to food bank charities.

“We’re giving Londoners a chance to stand up to far-right hatred and billionaires and express how they feel about the current state of the world,” said the group. “Therapy is expensive, but this is free.”

[‘I’m selling the Nazi mobile’: Tesla owners offload cars after Musk’s fascist-style salutes Read more](https://www.theguardian.com/technology/ng-interactive/2025/mar/02/tesla-owners-selling-musk)

Talia Denisenko, a 32-year-old writer, wore a Ukrainian flag as she took a hammer to the car’s bonnet as Britney Spears’s Hit Me Baby One More Time blared from a speaker. “My family is Ukrainian and Elon Musk wants to keep us occupied,” she said. “Things feel very disempowering at the moment. This is a little bit of therapy.”

Alice Rogers, a 24-year-old University of Cambridge researcher from Illinois, said: “Musk is acting in ways which violate our constitution. I’m very concerned by what I’m seeing – he’s gutting agencies and cutting USAID. This felt really cathartic. I’m not normally a smasher, but that felt really good.”

![Image 3: A man wearing a protective helmet stands on the bonnet of the car and smashes the windscreen with a sledgehammer. A banner behind the car says ‘everyone hates Elon’](https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/13c48fe742fb17b3fa8f2190ebe91045f418d842/0_0_5000_3000/master/5000.jpg?width=445&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none)[View image in fullscreen](https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2025/apr/10/sledgehammer-wielding-musk-critics-smash-up-tesla-in-london-art-project#img-2)

A spokesperson for Everyone Hates Elon said it was giving people a chance to express how they feel about the state of the world. Photograph: Henry Nicholls/AFP/Getty Images

Everyone Hates Elon, which garnered attention this year for distributing stickers with the slogan “Don’t buy a Swasticar”, said it had made clear that the stunt, called London vs Musk, should not be replicated outside the event.

“This is a private event with a used Tesla that was destined for the scrapyard – it’s a supervised, controlled art piece and there are proper safety measures in place,” said a spokesperson. “We urge people not to damage other Teslas or any other cars.”

The battery of the scrap car had been removed and recycled.

“I’m just aghast at what I see going on in America at the moment,” said Lee Woods, a 45-year-old university lecturer who had travelled two hours from Hampshire for the event. “I think Musk is using his obscene wealth to promote the far right.”

Musk, the world’s richest person, leads the Trump administration’s “department of government efficiency” (Doge), which the president tasked with drastically reducing US government jobs and cutting national debt.

![Image 4: Two men, one with sledgehammer and one with a baseball bat, take swings at the car](https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/7de22769b6b104c8eef2c27f8e5ed2e7b4c6546d/0_56_5000_3000/master/5000.jpg?width=445&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none)[View image in fullscreen](https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2025/apr/10/sledgehammer-wielding-musk-critics-smash-up-tesla-in-london-art-project#img-3)

Protests calling for a boycott of Tesla have been taking place on both sides of the Atlantic. Photograph: Henry Nicholls/AFP/Getty Images

Tesla’s shares dropped 13% in the first three months of 2025 – an indication of buyer backlash as a result of Musk’s rightwing politics. Protests calling for a boycott of the electric vehicle company have been taking place on both sides of the Atlantic in recent months, including a global day of action where hundreds of Tesla branches were targeted by protesters from the US group Tesla Takedown.

“My opinion \[on Musk\] has changed hugely,” said Giles Pearson, 32, who dealt the first blow on Thursday. “Since buying Twitter he’s become seriously rightwing and alienated a lot of people by doing so. I would never normally do something like this … but I’ve always wanted to smash a car.”

Tesla was approached for comment.

Jeff Bezos alters Venice wedding plans after threat of inflatable crocodiles
============================================================================

This article is more than 5 months old

Amazon founder reportedly forced to change venue for his wedding celebrations in Italian city

*   [Tell us: are you getting married in Venice this weekend?](https://www.theguardian.com/world/2025/jun/24/tell-us-are-you-getting-married-in-venice-this-weekend-italy-jeff-bezos-lauren-sanchez)
    

[Angela Giuffrida](https://www.theguardian.com/profile/angela-giuffrida) in Venice

Tue 24 Jun 2025 20.14 BSTFirst published on Tue 24 Jun 2025 16.36 BST

[Share](mailto:?subject=JeffBezosaltersVeniceweddingplansafterthreatofinflatablecrocodiles&body=https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2025/jun/24/jeff-bezos-lauren-sanchez-change-wedding-reception-location-in-venice-after-threatened-protest?CMP=share_btn_url)

Campaigners in Venice have claimed victory after [Jeff Bezos](https://www.theguardian.com/technology/jeff-bezos) was reportedly forced to change the venue for his wedding celebrations in the city as his guests started arriving on Tuesday for the three-day jamboree.

The main reception for the [wedding of Bezos and Lauren Sánchez](https://www.theguardian.com/world/2025/jun/14/venice-worn-out-jeff-bezos-wedding-overtourism), a former TV journalist, was due to be held in the Scuola Grande della Misericordia, a majestic 16th-century building in the city centre.

But according to the [No Space for Bezos](https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2025/jun/24/inside-the-no-space-for-bezos-movement-one-man-rents-a-city-for-three-days-thats-obscene) group, the couple relented after activists threatened to fill the canals with inflatable crocodiles to block their celebrity guests from entering.

![Image 3: The canal outside the Scuola Grande della Misericordia](https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/ccb224f1e19ab98adda37812012e5be50fe6fec8/0_0_5500_3668/master/5500.jpg?width=445&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none)[View image in fullscreen](https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2025/jun/24/jeff-bezos-lauren-sanchez-change-wedding-reception-location-in-venice-after-threatened-protest#img-2)

The Scuola Grande della Misericordia**,** a 16th-century building in the centre of Venice. Photograph: Yara Nardi/Reuters

The event will instead take place in Arsenale, a historic complex of shipyards surrounded by fortified walls that will be much harder for the protesters to penetrate.

According to local press reports, the venue switch was also due to security concerns after the US joined the war between Israel and Iran, especially because Donald Trump’s daughter, Ivanka, arrived in [Venice](https://www.theguardian.com/world/venice) on Tuesday.

[Inside the No Space for Bezos movement: ‘One man rents a city for three days? That’s obscene’ Read more](https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2025/jun/24/inside-the-no-space-for-bezos-movement-one-man-rents-a-city-for-three-days-thats-obscene)

The authorities in Venice have upped security across the city, particularly in the Jewish neighbourhood.

The 200 or so wedding guests, who may also include Elon Musk, Kim Kardashian and Leonardo DiCaprio, will arrive in Venice on Tuesday and Wednesday. An estimated 95 private planes are reported to be landing at the city’s airport.

No precise dates or details have been confirmed, although it is believed the celebrations will begin on Thursday, with the couple exchanging vows on Friday in San Giorgio Maggiore basilica on the Venetian island of the same name. The big party is expected to be held on Saturday.

Activists said that instead of trying to stop the wedding, they will organise a “no Bezos, no war” march.

“We feel as if we scored a victory,” said one activist, who asked not to be named. “The crocodile initiative would have given a bad impression of the city – this is why the venue was changed even if the authorities might try to claim it was because of the war.”

![Image 4: San Giorgio Maggiore](https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/be0c546d3a8c436279ce77d74689fabc2184713e/0_0_4461_3047/master/4461.jpg?width=445&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none)[View image in fullscreen](https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2025/jun/24/jeff-bezos-lauren-sanchez-change-wedding-reception-location-in-venice-after-threatened-protest#img-3)

San Giorgio Maggiore, where Bezos and Sánchez are expected to exchange vows on Friday. Photograph: Yara Nardi/Reuters

The campaign group emerged soon after Venice’s millionaire mayor, Luigi Brugnaro, confirmed in March that the [couple would be getting married in the city](https://www.theguardian.com/world/2025/mar/28/a-great-big-nuisance-venetians-divided-over-plans-to-host-jeff-bezos-wedding). Protesters say the event risks turning the world heritage site, which has long suffered from the effects of excessive tourism, into a playground for the rich.

Posters featuring an image of Bezos’s head on a rocket blasting into space – in reference to his Blue Origin space tourism venture – have appeared across the city.

Greenpeace Italia and the British activist group Everyone Hates Elon have also joined the protests, unfurling a huge banner in St Mark’s Square on Monday with a picture of Bezos laughing and a sign reading: “If you can rent Venice for your wedding you can pay more tax.”

Greenpeace said the initiative was aimed at highlighting the “social and climate injustice” of such events.

![Image 5: A large banner that says ‘If you can rent Venice for your wedding you can pay more tax’ above a picture of Bezos laughing](https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/058355173a3c4fbb1e5a3ab853b2b7789fa372ad/0_70_5500_3544/master/5500.jpg?width=445&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none)[View image in fullscreen](https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2025/jun/24/jeff-bezos-lauren-sanchez-change-wedding-reception-location-in-venice-after-threatened-protest#img-4)

A banner in St Mark’s Square unfurled by Greenpeace Italia and Everyone Hates Elon. Photograph: Yara Nardi/Reuters

“Bezos embodies an economic and social model that is leading us towards collapse,” Greenpeace said, arguing that lifestyles fuelled by “the arrogance of a few billionaires” are devastating for the planet.

Brugnaro said he was ashamed of those who protest against people who “bring riches” to the city.

Eyeing an opportunity amid the controversy, Matteo Pressi, the mayor of Soàve, a walled village in Veneto with a population of about 7,000, said he had written to Amazon Italia inviting the couple to host their nuptials there instead.

“Venice is unique, but getting married in the most beautiful village in [Italy](https://www.theguardian.com/world/italy) wouldn’t be so bad either,” he said.

Huge Trump and Epstein photograph unveiled outside Windsor Castle ahead of state visit

*   A giant picture of [Donald Trump](https://www.independent.co.uk/topic/donald-trump) and [Jeffrey Epstein](https://www.independent.co.uk/topic/jeffrey-epstein) was unveiled outside [Windsor Castle](https://www.independent.co.uk/topic/windsor-castle).
*   The political campaign group Everyone Hates Elon unfurled the image ahead of the [US](https://www.independent.co.uk/topic/us) president's visit to the [UK](https://www.independent.co.uk/topic/uk).
*   The group stated the picture was crowdfunded by the British public to highlight the Epstein story.
*   The US president is scheduled to be hosted by [The King](https://www.independent.co.uk/topic/the-king) at Windsor Castle for a ceremonial welcome and state banquet.
*   Watch the video in full above.

Van showing Trump and Epstein picture driven round Aberdeen as US president visits Scotland
===========================================================================================

A van displaying a picture of [Donald Trump](https://www.independent.co.uk/topic/donald-trump) and [Jeffrey Epstein](https://www.independent.co.uk/topic/jeffrey-epstein) on its side was driven around Aberdeen, a video posted to Instagram by the [Everyone Hates Elon political campaign group](https://www.independent.co.uk/tv/news/trump-epstein-protest-scotland-visit-video-b2793690.html) on Monday (28 July) shows.

The video was posted as the US president spoke with Sir [Keir Starmer](https://www.independent.co.uk/topic/keir-starmer) at his Turnberry golf course ball room in South Ayrshire.

Mr Trump and the prime minister met to discuss the UK-US trade deal as Britain hopes to be spared from the president’s tariff regime.

Footage showed the vehicle passing Marischal College in the city centre.

The company reported earnings on Jan. 29, and the stock has declined by as much as 15% since. So far, in 2025, the stock has generated a negative return of 12% (as of market close on Feb. 14).

While it is true that [sales in Tesla's core electric vehicle (EV) segment are decelerating](https://www.fool.com/investing/2025/02/15/prediction-tesla-stock-could-plunge-another-50-mor/), I think there is a more subtle reason for the sell-off. Below, I'm going to explore what I see as the root of the shares' decline and make the case for why now is a good opportunity to [buy the dip](https://www.fool.com/terms/b/buy-the-dip/).

Is Elon getting too comfy in Washington?
----------------------------------------

The chart below illustrates the fluctuations in Tesla's share price from Oct. 1 through Feb. 14. Notice anything?

Starting in early November, Tesla stock went on an epically bullish ride that propelled it to new all-time highs just as 2024 came to a close. One of the tailwinds that fueled the stock during the final weeks of 2024 was Donald Trump's win in the presidential election. Elon Musk was a big supporter of then-candidate Trump, and many investors simply assumed that his [relationship with the president would bode well for Tesla's future](https://www.fool.com/investing/2025/01/08/down-18-from-all-time-highs-is-the-trump-joyride-o/) -- especially as it relates to any regulatory hurdles for the company's ambitions with self-driving vehicles.

Why this sell-off is overblown
------------------------------

On the surface, I can understand if investors are wary that Musk is allocating too much of his time to DOGE as opposed to dedicating every moment to Tesla. However, the argument that he may be distracted is flawed for a couple of reasons.

First, he is a serial entrepreneur who has been at the center of a [number of successful businesses](https://www.fool.com/investing/how-to-invest/famous-investors/elon-musk-investments/). Beyond Tesla, he is the CEO of [SpaceX](https://www.fool.com/investing/how-to-invest/stocks/how-to-invest-in-spacex-stock/) and founded a number of billion-dollar start-ups including Neuralink, which is developing chips that are implantable in human brains; The Boring Company, a tunnel builder; and xAI, an artificial intelligence specialist. He also owns social media platform X (formerly Twitter) and is its executive chairman.

Is now a good time to buy Tesla stock?
--------------------------------------

Tesla is a stock that has always traded out of the bounds of traditional valuation metrics. The company has accelerated sales and profits in recent years, and the stock trades in an entirely different universe when compared to other automakers.

[![Image 16: TSLA PS Ratio Chart](https://media.ycharts.com/charts/3ca4c26a951819562c5e485b8494f37f.png)](https://ycharts.com/companies/TSLA/chart/)

[TSLA PS ratio,](https://ycharts.com/companies/TSLA/ps_ratio) data by [YCharts; PS = price to sales.](https://ycharts.com/)

I've made the case in the past that Tesla is really a technology company that happens to sell cars. It's investing heavily in an autonomous vehicle fleet as well as dedicating a good portion of its artificial intelligence (AI) budget to [Optimus humanoid robots](https://www.fool.com/investing/2025/02/08/elon-musk-just-said-tesla-has-a-10-trillion-opport/), so Musk has a vision for Tesla well beyond EVs.

For these reasons, I've always thought that it's a little dicey driving your investment decision in Tesla based purely on valuation metrics. To me, the ongoing sell-off is disconnected from the fundamentals of the business.

The core operations of the company do need a new jump-start, but I think this is quite possible over the next several years, especially given his relationship with President Trump. For now, I wouldn't worry too much about Musk's focus on DOGE. If you're an investor with a long-term horizon, I think now is a good opportunity to take advantage of Tesla's low stock price.

Colin is an Associate Editor focused on tech and financial news. He has more than three years of experience editing, proofreading, and fact-checking content on current financial events and politics. He received his M.A. in journalism from The New School and his B.A. in history and political science from McGill University.

04:59 PM EDT

![Image 3: Elon Musk, chief executive officer of Tesla Inc., during a cabinet meeting at the White House.](https://www.investopedia.com/thmb/sarXu18xEIWPdTAv8dIj9Rzdsbs=/1500x0/filters:no_upscale():max_bytes(150000):strip_icc():format(webp)/GettyImages-2206215134-3929637d8594486ba74ef38fdf3d01ee.jpg)

Samuel Corum / Sipa / Bloomberg via Getty Images

Close

### Key Takeaways

*   Tesla shares fell 5.6% on Wednesday, ending the stock's five-day rally from a prolonged slump.
*   The stock had gained more than 27% in the week leading up to Wednesday's session, boosted by the potential for watered-down tariffs and several endorsements.
*   William Blair analysts on Wednesday slashed their full-year vehicle sales forecast but maintained an outperform rating on the stock, citing opportunities outside Tesla's core EV business and the likelihood dip-buyers lend the stock upward momentum.

Tesla ([TSLA](https://www.investopedia.com/markets/quote?tvwidgetsymbol=TSLA)) shares fell 5.6% on Wednesday, ending the EV maker's rebound from a prolonged slump.

Tesla shares rose more than 27% in the five sessions leading up to today's. The climb marked their best stretch of that length since investors bid up the stock in the wake of Trump’s November election victory.

Before beginning to rally last week, Tesla's shares were down more than 50% from their all-time highs set in December, with much of that decline coming throughout February and early March. Tesla’s sales in key markets, like Europe, [have slumped this year](https://www.investopedia.com/tesla-eu-sales-tumble-again-even-as-overall-ev-registrations-rise-11702769) despite rising demand for electric vehicles. Tesla cars and dealerships have been targeted by vandals upset with CEO Elon Musk’s political influence. And ardent bulls have publicly worried that Musk is [stretched too thin](https://www.investopedia.com/wedbush-analysts-say-musk-needs-to-announce-he-will-balance-doge-and-being-tesla-ceo-11700385) by his corporate and government work.

But the price of Tesla's stock at times appears to have little connection to the health of its EV business, a disconnect that was apparent Wednesday when William Blair analysts cut their full-year vehicle sales estimate by more than 10% while maintaining their outperform rating on the stock.

“Despite the correction in the auto business near term, we remain positive on the faster-than-expected ramp of the Megapack business and ride-sharing rolling out this year,” the analysts wrote.1 (Megapack is Tesla’s industrial-scale energy storage product.)

Trading Tesla stock, the analysts said, has often "been a function of momentum." For that reason, they argue the stock's significant pullback is a reason for optimism in and of itself. “We believe expectations are near a bottom, and as they reset, shares will bottom and momentum will rebound,” the analysts wrote.

What's Saved Tesla's Stock From Free Fall?
------------------------------------------

Musk and his allies have undertaken a damage control campaign this month. President Trump two weeks ago told his followers on Truth Social that [he would buy a Tesla](https://www.investopedia.com/trump-is-buying-a-tesla-11694571) as a show of support for Musk. He subsequently held a press conference on the White House South Lawn where he inspected five Tesla vehicles and praised Musk.

Last Wednesday, Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick urged Americans to buy Tesla stock during a TV appearance.

“It's unbelievable that this guy's stock is this cheap. It'll never be this cheap again,” Lutnick told _Fox News_.2 The following day, Musk urged employees to [hold onto their stock](https://www.investopedia.com/elon-musk-told-tesla-workers-to-hang-on-the-stock-rose-today-11701154) during an all-hands meeting.

Tesla's latest winning streak began last Wednesday after the Federal Reserve updated its economic outlook, in which officials forecast [cutting interest rates twice](https://www.investopedia.com/dot-plot-spotlight-fed-sees-interest-rate-cuts-coming-11699946) this year. And stocks got a boost early this week from reports that the Trump administration is [considering limiting the tariffs](https://www.investopedia.com/trump-walks-back-reciprocal-tariff-threat-11701975) it plans to roll out on April 2.

Retail investors have been eager to buy the dip, reportedly piling into Tesla stock at a record pace during its recent slump.3
